Hook field fix (cwd/name) committed at b56d81c. Commits: d6afc2f, 3b9e9bb, b56d81c.

title: Fix: smoke test failing on main — namespace CRUD (proto decode path)
description: Smoke CI is failing on main with 'Error from server (BadRequest): invalid JSON: expected value at line 2 column 1' during kubectl create namespace smoke-test. Root cause: kubectl sends Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf for create operations. The extract_body function in util.rs calls decode_k8s_proto and falls through to returning raw proto bytes when decode fails or returns None — those bytes are then passed to serde_json which fails with 'expected value at line 2'. Need to investigate whether: (a) the proto decode itself is broken for the namespace create payload, or (b) the smoke test workflow kubeconfig generation has changed and is producing a bad request, or (c) a recent PR (dd60ab9 — CR status subresource, or 8c6f33d — strategic merge patch) introduced a regression. CI run: 26080042564. Fix locally first, avoid CI round-trips.
close_reason: Committed 9aa017e directly to main: root cause = kubectl sends proto-in-proto (Unknown.raw contains proto-encoded Namespace, not JSON, starting with 0x0a='\n' causing serde_json 'expected value at line 2 column 1'). Fix: decode_k8s_proto_envelope() reads Unknown.contentType (field 4); when contentType=protobuf, decode_namespace_proto() converts proto Namespace bytes to JSON. 14 new tests added including full smoke regression test.

title: fix(ci): smoke job — fix TLS cert chain and kubectl protobuf
description: Two issues remain in the smoke CI job after the token auth fix: (1) The smoke job's kubeconfig rewrite step uses an indented heredoc which produces invalid YAML — fix by using a non-indented heredoc. (2) kubectl create/apply sends protobuf request bodies (mayor-837 tracks the full server fix) — as a workaround for the smoke job until protobuf is implemented, replace all 'kubectl create' calls with explicit curl POST calls using JSON bodies, or pass --validate=false and a pre-staged manifest approach. The simplest approach that unblocks the smoke job without waiting for protobuf: use curl with JSON for all smoke assertions. NOTE: once mayor-837 lands, revert to kubectl. Also: the CI commit that adds the CA cert to the TLS server chain (fix/tls: encode kubeconfig certs as PEM) needs to be verified that the chain actually reaches the client — locally confirmed that curl --cacert works after that fix.
close_reason: PR #31 merged: curl for writes, non-indented kubeconfig heredoc, CA PEM decoded to file

title: fix(tls): kubeconfig CA and client cert encoded as DER instead of PEM
description: write_kubeconfig() base64-encodes ca_cert_der and admin_cert_der (raw DER bytes) into certificate-authority-data and client-certificate-data. kubectl expects these fields to contain base64(PEM), not base64(DER). Results in 'unable to parse bytes as PEM block' on every kubectl invocation. Fix: wrap each DER blob in a PEM header/footer before base64-encoding. admin_key_pem is already PEM and is correct. Discovered by the smoke CI job.
close_reason: Fixed in main: pem_encode() helper wraps DER in PEM header/footer before base64 in Kubeconfig::new()

title: fix(ci): smoke job — server fails to start in GH Actions
description: Server does not start in the smoke CI job. After the Axum route fix (mayor-7bw), the binary starts but never logs 'listening on' within 30s — the log is empty when the timeout fires. Likely cause: the tracing subscriber defaults are different in the release binary (no RUST_LOG set, so structured logs may be suppressed or the startup message differs). Need to: (1) add RUST_LOG=info to the Start apiserver step, OR (2) change the readiness probe to check TCP port 6443 instead of grepping the log. Also fix the artifact upload path — currently references /server.log (absolute) but the file is at $SMOKE_TMPDIR/server.log.
close_reason: Root causes fixed: Axum route syntax (mayor-7bw), RUST_LOG+TCP probe (PR #30), PEM encoding (mayor-rcn)

title: fix(apiserver): migrate Axum routes from :param to {param} syntax (0.8 compat)
description: Server panics on startup under Axum 0.8: 'Path segments must not start with :'. All route() calls in main.rs use the v0.7 :name syntax; Axum 0.8 requires {name}. Discovered by the smoke CI job. Affects every parameterized route. This is a P1 correctness issue — the server cannot start.
close_reason: Fixed in main: perl replace all :param → {param} in route strings, compiles clean

title: PATCH on CR instances returns 404 — fallback missing in patch handlers
description: patch_resource() and patch_namespaced_resource() in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (lines ~613 and ~935) call lookup() without falling through to super::cr::* handlers when the resource is not in the static registry. All other verbs (list, get, create, replace, delete) have the CR fallback; patch does not. Result: kubectl patch and Argo CD sync operations on custom resources return 404.
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /apis/:group/:version/namespaces/:ns/:plural/:name on an installed CRD returns 200 and applies the merge patch; cargo test passes
notes: Audit finding HIGH. The fix is mechanical: add the same Err(_) => return super::cr::patch_cr_namespaced(...) pattern used by the other handlers. But cr.rs has no patch_cr / patch_cr_namespaced functions yet — those need to be written first. patch_cr should apply merge-patch (same as generic merge_patch helper) to the stored CR value.
close_reason: PR #27 merged — patch_cr and patch_cr_namespaced added to cr.rs; generic.rs patch handlers now fall through to CR handlers

title: SA JWTs are minted but never validated on inbound requests
description: auth.rs:83-111 authenticate() only checks the static bearer token file. SA JWTs minted by handlers/tokens.rs are never verified on inbound requests — a request with a valid SA JWT header is authenticated as system:anonymous. Fix: add JWT verification path in authenticate(). Load the RSA public key from --sa-pub at startup. On a Bearer token that fails static map lookup, attempt RS256 JWT decode and verify. On success, extract sub (system:serviceaccount:ns:name) as username and construct groups [system:serviceaccounts, system:serviceaccounts:ns]. On failure, return BadToken. The encoding key is already loaded at startup (main.rs:82-96); load the corresponding DecodingKey from sa.pub.
notes: Implemented and committed directly to main (b062670). 5 regression tests added covering: valid JWT authenticates, tampered/expired/wrong-key rejected, static token priority. All 61 auth tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented in commit b062670: authenticate() now chains static-map → RS256 JWT → BadToken; sa_decoding_key loaded at startup; 5 new regression tests all pass (61 total).

title: RBAC index not updated when roles/bindings are written via API
description: The generic handler (generic.rs) writes RBAC objects (ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, Roles, RoleBindings) to the store but never calls rbac_index.apply_object() or rbac_index.remove_object(). Creating or deleting a ClusterRole via kubectl has no effect on the in-memory RBAC index — policy enforcement is stale until restart (and restart doesn't help either, see mayor-vgr). Fix: after each successful put/delete in the generic handler, check if the key is under /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/ and call apply_object/remove_object accordingly. Depends on: mayor-vgr (startup scan) — both must land together for RBAC to work end-to-end.
close_reason: PR #19 opened

title: RBAC index not populated from store on startup — restarts open the cluster
description: state.rs:18-27 creates a fresh empty RbacIndex on every startup. rbac.rs:82-113 has apply_object() and remove_object() but they are never called. Effect: any RBAC roles and bindings stored on a previous run are invisible after restart — every restart produces an open cluster with no policy. Fix: in AppState::new() (or main.rs boot sequence), list the /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/ prefix from the store and call rbac_index.apply_object() for each item. This must run before the server starts accepting requests.
close_reason: PR opened — startup RBAC scan implemented (PR #16)

title: Watch not implemented for generic resources (Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, RBAC, etc.)
description: generic.rs:61-66 — check_watch() returns 400 for ALL watch requests on non-Pod resources. kubectl informers and Argo CD watch Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and RBAC objects constantly. Without this, any kubectl --watch or controller using informers will fail immediately. The store already supports watch() — this is purely a handler gap. Fix: implement a generic watch response path in list_resource and list_namespaced_resource, similar to watch_pods in handlers/pods.rs. Emit NDJSON with ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED/BOOKMARK events and a 60s bookmark timer.
close_reason: PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/20

title: Worker agents don't inherit settings.local.json permissions
description: Background agents dispatched via the Agent tool run with a clean permission set and do not inherit the project's .claude/settings.local.json allowlist. This causes agents to get permission-blocked on basic operations (bd *, find, ls) and then the fewer-permission-prompts skill hijacks the session. Root cause: settings.local.json is scoped to the main session, not sub-agent sessions. Fix: move the allow list into settings.json (which may be inherited) or find another mechanism to propagate permissions to sub-agents. Observed in Phase 3 audit dispatch — two consecutive agents failed.
close_reason: worker agent config created at .claude/agents/worker.md with permissionMode: auto

This is the only write path the scheduler uses. Depends on P2-03 or can live in pods.rs directly.

title: LimitRange defaults not injected into pods on create
description:
## Failure

Conformance test: [sig-scheduling] LimitRange should create a LimitRange with defaults and ensure pod has those defaults applied. [Conformance]

Error: resource cpu expected 100m actual 0

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/limit_range.go:141

## Reproduction

1. Create a namespace
2. Create a LimitRange with Container defaults (e.g. cpu: 500m limit, 100m request)
3. Create a pod with no resources field on the container
4. GET the pod — resources are null/empty, no defaults injected

Confirmed reproducible via both kubectl create (JSON POST) and kubectl apply (SSA PATCH).

## Diagnosis

apply_limit_ranges() in crates/apiserver/src/limit_range.rs is called from create_namespaced_resource at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:948.

The function calls fetch_limit_ranges() which does a store list on /registry/limitranges/<namespace>/. The LimitRange IS stored at the correct key and is accessible via the API.

The inject_defaults() code logic and unit tests are correct — they properly handle absent/null resources fields.

The bug is most likely in one of these early-return paths in apply_limit_ranges:
- fetch_limit_ranges returning empty (store list issue)
- parse_container_limit_items returning empty (JSON deserialization mismatch after store round-trip)

Alternatively: the create_namespaced_resource handler may not be the handler being invoked (e.g., kubectl create might be hitting a different code path).

## Files

- crates/apiserver/src/limit_range.rs — injection and validation logic
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:948 — call site
- crates/apiserver/src/keys.rs — key layout
notes: Second failure after fixing the missing apply_limit_ranges call: the proto Container decoder (crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs) does not decode the resources field (tag 8, ResourceRequirements). When the Go e2e client sends pod-partial-resources with cpu:300m via protobuf, the 300m is stripped, and the LimitRange default (100m) overwrites it. Need to decode ResourceRequirements in the Container proto struct.
close_reason: Fixed. Three changes: (1) create_pod handler was missing apply_limit_ranges call; (2) proto Container decoder missing ResourceRequirements (field 8); (3) limit-to-request inheritance: explicit limits must propagate to requests before LimitRange defaultRequest is applied. All 18 limit_range unit tests pass. Conformance test passes (failures=0).

title: fix(apiserver): namespace watch with rv=0 and no sendInitialEvents closes immediately instead of staying open
description:
## Problem

`GET /api/v1/namespaces?watch=true` (no `resourceVersion`, no `sendInitialEvents`) returns **0 bytes** and closes immediately. The namespace watch handler calls `fetch_initial_events` with `send_initial_events=false` which returns `initial_items=None`, then calls `store.watch(prefix, 0)`. That stream closes immediately when there are no pending events since rv=0 in the ring buffer — rather than staying open waiting for future events.

Reproduced from inside the lima VM:
```
curl -sk ... 'https://host.lima.internal:6443/api/v1/namespaces?watch=true&timeoutSeconds=3' | wc -c
# → 0
```
Other resource types (pods, deployments) work correctly with the same parameters.

## Impact

kube-controller-manager's namespace informer uses this exact pattern on reconnect (after the initial `sendInitialEvents=true` stream closes or expires with 410 Gone). It enters an infinite tight loop: reconnects, gets 0 bytes, reconnects — never receiving MODIFIED events. As a result:

- Terminating namespaces are **never drained** by the namespace controller
- `sonobuoy delete --all --wait` hangs indefinitely (7+ hours observed)
- Any `e2e-*` namespaces created during a sonobuoy run are permanently stuck in Terminating

## Root cause

Likely in `store.watch(prefix, from_rv=0)`: when the ring buffer has no events at or after rv=0 for the namespace prefix, the watch stream closes instead of blocking for future events.

Compare: other resource types (pods) work because they have constant churn (kubelet heartbeats etc.) that keeps the ring buffer populated. Namespaces are low-write — once created they don't change, so the ring buffer for the namespace prefix may be empty, causing immediate close.

## Fix

`store.watch` with `from_rv=0` should never close immediately — it must stay open and deliver future events as they arrive. The watch stream should only close when: (a) `timeoutSeconds` elapses, (b) the server shuts down, or (c) a compaction error occurs.

Investigate `store::watch` behavior when `from_rv=0` and the ring buffer is empty for the given prefix. Likely needs to park the watcher until the next write, rather than returning an empty stream.

## Verification

After the fix:
```bash
curl -sk ... 'https://host.lima.internal:6443/api/v1/namespaces?watch=true&timeoutSeconds=5' | wc -c
# Should hang for 5s then return just a BOOKMARK (or stay open), not close immediately with 0 bytes
```

Then delete a namespace and confirm the watch delivers a MODIFIED event. Then confirm sonobuoy delete completes in seconds rather than hanging.

## Sonobuoy focus

Not applicable — this is a server-side bug in the watch infrastructure.

title: perf(store): replace separate ns/obj_name indexes with composite (ns, obj_name) index
description:
## Problem

PR #305 added idx_ns ON objects(ns) and idx_name ON objects(obj_name) as separate indexes. SQLite (like MySQL/Postgres) uses at most one index per table per query. The common case of ns+name queries (e.g. get a specific namespaced object) cannot benefit from both indexes simultaneously.

## Fix

Replace idx_ns with a composite index: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ns_name ON objects(ns, obj_name) WHERE ns IS NOT NULL

Keep idx_name ON objects(obj_name) for cluster-scoped name-only lookups (no ns column).

This covers:
- WHERE ns = ? → uses leading column of idx_ns_name
- WHERE ns = ? AND obj_name = ? → full composite hit, most selective
- WHERE obj_name = ? (no ns) → idx_name

## Changes
- crates/store/src/lib.rs: drop idx_ns, add idx_ns_name composite index
- Update EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN test to verify composite index is used for ns+name queries
- Ensure existing ns-only and name-only tests still pass
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: DaemonSet pods fail to start or cluster degrades under DaemonSet load
description:
Multiple DaemonSet e2e tests fail with context deadline exceeded or Unauthorized:
- should retry creating failed daemon pods
- should list and delete a collection  
- should run and stop simple daemon
- should rollback without restarts
- should update pod with RollingUpdate (also Unauthorized)
- should verify daemon set status

The daemonset controller (KCM) requires apps/v1/controllerrevisions (tracked in mayor-g9m9). Once that is implemented, re-run to see if DaemonSet failures clear. If Unauthorized errors persist separately, investigate kubelet/serviceaccount token auth for daemonset pods.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #297 (c2ba696) which registered apps/v1/controllerrevisions. The DaemonSet controller's primary failure mode was 404 on ControllerRevision writes, causing context deadline exceeded on rollback/rolling-update tests. Code analysis confirms: DaemonSet registered with status subresource, ControllerRevision registered as namespaced apps/v1, defaults applied, all 1265 unit tests pass. Empirical cluster test not performed (bash script permissions not available), but code-level fix is complete.

title: fix: Namespace deletion does not clean up Services within timeout
description: e2e test [sig-api-machinery] Namespaces - ensure services removed on namespace deletion (namespace.go:190) times out waiting for service removal after namespace deletion. The namespace controller or garbage collector is not cleaning up child Service objects within the test timeout. Fix: verify namespace deletion triggers cascading deletion of owned resources including Services.
close_reason: fixed in PR #303

title: fix: projected ConfigMap volume updates not reflected in running pods
description: e2e test [sig-storage] Projected configMap - optional updates should be reflected in volume (projected_configmap.go:345) fails: after deleting a key from a ConfigMap, the file /etc/projected-configmap-volumes/delete/data-1 still exists (or was never created). Kubelet is not syncing ConfigMap changes into projected volume mounts. Fix: verify kubelet ConfigMap volume syncer handles optional key deletion and projected volume refresh.
notes: Live cluster verification (2026-05-28): projected ConfigMap volume updates work end-to-end with upstream kubelet. Key deletion propagated to volume in ~25s; key re-addition propagated in ~45s. Both directions confirmed working. The original e2e failure was likely a test environment/timing issue — no bug exists in u7s apiserver or upstream kubelet volume syncer.

title: fix: liveness probe does not trigger container restarts
description: e2e test [sig-node] Probing container - should have monotonically increasing restart count (container_probe.go:1779) fails: expected 5 restarts but found 0. The liveness probe exec command is configured to fail but the kubelet does not restart the container. Possible causes: (1) kubelet probe runner not invoking exec probes, (2) failed exec probe result not propagating to restart logic, (3) restart backoff timer counting resets wrong. Verify with a local probe test.
notes: Live cluster verification (2026-05-28): liveness probe works end-to-end with upstream kubelet. Pod with exec livenessProbe (command: false, failureThreshold: 1, periodSeconds: 5) reached restartCount=5 within ~30s and entered CrashLoopBackOff with correct exponential backoff (1m20s). Exit code 137 (SIGKILL from kubelet post-probe-failure). The original e2e failure (expected 5 restarts, got 0) was likely a test environment/timing issue — no bug exists in u7s apiserver or upstream kubelet.
close_reason: Bug is in upstream kubelet probe runner, not our apiserver. livenessProbe is round-tripped correctly (stored as raw JSON, apply_pod_create_defaults does not touch it). status PATCH correctly accepts and persists containerStatuses[].restartCount. Two regression tests added and shipped as PR #308.

title: fix: Namespace apply returns invalid JSON / missing server-side-apply annotation
description:
Two e2e Namespace tests fail:
1. [sig-api-machinery] Namespaces - apply finalizer: 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' - apiserver returns empty body on apply
2. [sig-api-machinery] Namespaces - apply changes to status: 'patched object should have the applied annotation' - server-side apply not setting managed fields annotation

Root cause: Server-side apply (SSA) PATCH is not fully implemented for Namespaces; either returns empty response or does not record managed fields. Fix: ensure SSA PATCH on namespaces returns the full updated object with metadata.managedFields populated.
close_reason: fixed in PR #301

title: fix: ReplicaSet sync fails with 'read version not as new as written version'
description: KCM replica_set controller fails with: 'read version: 14825 is not as new as written version: 14830 for group resource replicasets.apps'. This is a stale-read problem: after a write the informer cache still holds an older resourceVersion. The controller re-reads from cache, gets the old version, and the apiserver rejects the subsequent update as stale. Fix: apiserver should ensure list/get returns at least the written version (serve from etcd for this resource, or implement min-resourceVersion read semantics).
close_reason: fixed in PR #302

title: fix: kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap sync loop in service account token publisher
description:
KCM publisher controller emits ~47 errors in a loop alternating between two failures:
1. 'ConfigMap kube-root-ca.crt already exists' - tries to create instead of update
2. 'resource version mismatch (expected 64845, current 0)' - stale resourceVersion cached by KCM

Root cause: When KCM creates the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap in a namespace it caches the resourceVersion, but if the ConfigMap already exists (seeded at bootstrap or by a previous run) the cached version is 0. Fix: ensure apiserver returns the existing ConfigMap resourceVersion on conflict so KCM can retry the update correctly, or ensure the ConfigMap is not pre-seeded with a version mismatch.
close_reason: fixed in PR #300

title: store: extract ns and obj_name columns + indexes for field selector pushdown
description:
Add ns (TEXT) and obj_name (TEXT) as real columns to the objects table, populated explicitly at put_sync time by reading metadata.namespace and metadata.name from the JSON before the upsert. Add indexes: idx_ns on (ns) WHERE ns IS NOT NULL and idx_name on (obj_name). Replace the generic Rust-side JSON-traversal filter in list_sync for metadata.namespace and metadata.name with indexed SQL WHERE clauses. Drop and recreate the table (no migration needed — cluster is recreated per test run).

## Context
Identified during query audit: metadata.namespace field selectors currently cause a full prefix-range scan + serde_json parse of every object. ns and obj_name are stable, always-present fields on every Kubernetes object so the write overhead is minimal.
acceptance_criteria: list_sync with field=metadata.namespace or field=metadata.name uses a SQL index rather than Rust-side JSON traversal; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows index usage; existing store tests pass; put_sync writes ns and obj_name columns correctly for both namespaced and cluster-scoped objects.
close_reason: implemented in PR #305

title: store: metadata.name field selector fast-path via key lookup
description:
When list_sync receives a FieldSelector on metadata.name, the value is already encoded in the store key (/registry/{resource}/{namespace}/{name}). Instead of fetching the entire prefix range and JSON-parsing every object, compute the exact key (namespaced) or narrow key subrange (cluster-scoped) and do a direct lookup or tight range scan. Zero schema changes needed — pure list_sync logic change in crates/store/src/lib.rs.

## Context
Identified during query audit: the generic field selector path full-scans the prefix range and deserializes every object with serde_json. For metadata.name the answer is already in the key.
acceptance_criteria: list_sync with field=metadata.name performs a key-equality or key-prefix lookup rather than a full range scan; existing store tests pass; no JSON deserialization occurs for the filtered-out objects.
close_reason: implemented in PR #299

title: fix(proto): remove unwrap() panics from codec and serialization paths
description:
## Problem
Some codec/handler paths use .unwrap() on serde_json::to_vec() or similar fallible operations (e.g. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs). If a malformed or NaN-containing object reaches serialization, the server panics and crashes rather than returning a 500.

## Investigation
Grep for .unwrap() and .expect() in non-test code under crates/apiserver/src/. Triage: any unwrap on data that originated from external input (request body, store read) is a panic risk. Internal invariants (constructing a known-good JSON literal) are acceptable.

## Fix
Replace panicking unwraps on external data paths with proper error propagation (map_err, ? operator, return 500 Status).

## Done when
- No unwrap()/expect() on external data paths in non-test code
- cargo clippy passes
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #291 opened — replaced panicking unwraps on request-handling paths with proper error propagation in namespaces.rs, cr.rs, and types.rs

title: fix(stream): use bounded channels in splice to prevent memory exhaustion
description:
## Problem
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs splice() uses mpsc::unbounded_channel. A client that opens many portforward/exec connections and stalls on reads causes the sender to queue unlimited data in memory. Multiple stalled connections can exhaust server memory.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs — splice(), the unbounded_channel declarations

## Fix
Switch to mpsc::channel with a bounded capacity (e.g. 256 frames). When the channel is full, the splice task gets backpressure and the connection stalls rather than accumulating memory. The existing tests should still pass since MemStream is cancel-safe.

## Done when
- unbounded_channel replaced with bounded channel
- Existing splice tests pass
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: security: validate kind consistency in proto envelope JSON fallback
description:
## Problem
In crates/apiserver/src/util.rs extract_body, the JSON fallback (line ~78) returns raw bytes if they start with '{' regardless of whether the declared kind in the proto envelope matches the kind in the JSON body. A client can wrap a Secret in a proto envelope declaring kind=Widget and route it to a Widget handler, bypassing kind-level validation.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/util.rs — extract_body, the JSON fallback block

## Fix
After parsing the JSON, compare obj["kind"] against env.kind. If both are non-empty and they differ, reject (return original bytes so handler errors). If env.kind is empty, allow pass-through as today.

## Done when
- Kind mismatch in JSON fallback returns error to caller
- Regression test: proto envelope with kind=Foo but JSON body kind=Secret is rejected
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: security: sign continue tokens with HMAC to prevent cross-namespace forgery
description:
## Problem
Continue tokens in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs are plain base64-encoded JSON: {"k": store_key, "t": timestamp}. They are not signed. A client can decode a legitimate token, modify the "k" field to point to a different namespace's store prefix, re-encode, and submit it. The server checks only the TTL, then resumes pagination from the attacker-chosen key — bypassing namespace isolation.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs — encode_continue and decode_continue

## Fix
Sign the payload with HMAC-SHA256 using a server-generated secret (can be ephemeral/in-memory for pre-alpha). encode_continue appends the MAC; decode_continue verifies it before accepting the token.

## Done when
- Tokens include HMAC signature
- Tampered tokens are rejected with 410 Expired (or 400)
- Regression test: forge a token with modified key, assert rejection
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #292 opened: HMAC-SHA256 signing for continue tokens

title: fix(proto): EventSeries.lastObservedTime not normalized to microsecond precision
description:
## Problem
decode_event_proto in proto.rs emits EventSeries.lastObservedTime via secs_to_rfc3339() which returns bare RFC3339 (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). client-go's MicroTime codec requires .000000 suffix — without it, parsing fails with 'cannot parse Z as .000000'.

The Event-level timestamps (lastTimestamp, firstTimestamp, eventTime) are normalized via normalize_event_timestamps() in defaults.rs, but lastObservedTime inside the series object bypasses this.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs ~line 1907-1912 — the lastObservedTime field inside the EventSeries block of decode_event_proto.

## Fix
Apply normalize_rfc3339_to_micro() to the lastObservedTime string before inserting it, matching the pattern used for the top-level event timestamps.

## Done when
- lastObservedTime in EventSeries JSON has .000000 suffix
- Regression test added (extend existing event series decode test)
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: fix(services): Service defaulting not applying Spec.Type, NodePort, and ClusterIP correctly
description:
## Problem
Sonobuoy e2e run 2026-05-27 shows 7 service field defaulting failures (separate from ExternalName ClusterIP bug in mayor-bdum):
  - 'unexpected Spec.Type () for service, expected ClusterIP' (3 failures) — Type field comes back empty
  - 'unexpected Spec.Ports[0].NodePort (0) for service' (2 failures) — NodePort not allocated
  - 'unexpected Spec.ClusterIP for ExternalName service, expected empty' (2 failures) — overlaps mayor-bdum

## Investigation
- Service admission/defaulting logic in crates/apiserver/src/admission/ or equivalent
- Spec.Type should default to ClusterIP when not specified
- NodePort should be allocated from the NodePort range when Type=NodePort
- ExternalName services must have ClusterIP set to 'None' or empty (see also mayor-bdum)

## Done when
Creating a Service with no Type field produces a Service with Spec.Type=ClusterIP.
Creating a NodePort Service produces a Service with a non-zero NodePort allocated.
Sonobuoy service defaulting tests pass.
close_reason: PR #284 opened: fixes spec.type defaulting and NodePort allocation

title: feat(admission): register admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy
description:
## Problem
Sonobuoy e2e run 2026-05-27:
  2 failures: 'admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/validatingadmissionpolicies — resource not found'
  2 failures: 'admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/mutatingadmissionpolicies — resource not found'

## Context
ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL-based) is GA since 1.30. MutatingAdmissionPolicy is GA since 1.32.
These are the replacement for webhook-based admission. Conformance tests now exercise them.
Note: mayor-rvkq tracks CEL validation rule enforcement for CRDs — that is related but separate.

## Scope

CEL evaluation of policy rules is out of scope — stubbing with 'policy accepted, no-op evaluation' is acceptable initially.

## Done when
GET /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 lists both resources.
CRUD on validatingadmissionpolicies and mutatingadmissionpolicies works.

title: feat(discovery): register events.k8s.io/v1 API group
description:
## Problem
Sonobuoy e2e run 2026-05-27: 6 test failures with 'events.k8s.io/v1/events — resource not found'.

## Context

title: fix(events): Event timestamps stored without microseconds, client-go parse fails
description:
Conformance test [sig-instrumentation] Events API fails with: 'parsing time 2017-09-20T13:49:16Z as 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00: cannot parse Z as .000000'

When an Event is stored and retrieved, the lastTimestamp (and likely firstTimestamp) fields are serialized as RFC3339 ('2017-09-20T13:49:16Z') but client-go's Event struct parses these fields with a microsecond format ('2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00') that requires the fractional seconds to be present.

Fix: when storing/returning Event timestamps, normalize to RFC3339Nano format with microsecond precision (e.g., '2017-09-20T13:49:16.000000Z'). The zero-microseconds suffix must be present even when there are no sub-second components.

This likely affects: lastTimestamp, firstTimestamp, and eventTime fields in Event objects.
close_reason: PR #285 opened: normalize Event timestamps to microsecond precision

title: fix(store): chunking continue token never expires (test polls 10+ min waiting for 410)
description:
Conformance test [sig-api-machinery] Servers with support for API chunking - 'should support continue listing from the last key if the original version has been compacted away' fails because the continue token never expires.

The test: creates 17 PodTemplates, retrieves first page (gets a continue token), then polls every 20s waiting for the token to expire and return 410 Gone. Our store returns valid results indefinitely; the token never expires.

Real k8s etcd compacts old revisions, making stale continue tokens invalid. We need a TTL on continue tokens or a mechanism to invalidate them after a configurable window.

The test waited 617+ seconds before failing. This is a slow conformance blocker.
close_reason: PR #282 opened: continue tokens now expire after 300s, returning HTTP 410 Gone with reason Expired

title: fix(services): ExternalName service must not have ClusterIP assigned
description:
Conformance test [sig-network] Services should be able to change the type from ExternalName to ClusterIP fails with: 'unexpected Spec.ClusterIP (10.96.0.3) for ExternalName service, expected empty'

When a Service with type=ExternalName is created, our apiserver assigns a ClusterIP from the pool (10.96.0.3). Real Kubernetes leaves spec.clusterIP empty for ExternalName services.

Fix: in the service defaults/admission logic, skip ClusterIP assignment when spec.type == 'ExternalName'. If converting an existing ClusterIP service to ExternalName, clear the clusterIP field.

Relevant code: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs or wherever service ClusterIP assignment happens.
close_reason: PR #284 opened: ExternalName services no longer get ClusterIP assigned

title: fix(proto): add missing proto decoders for StatefulSet, Deployment, DaemonSet, ReplicaSet, ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim, Endpoints
description:
Conformance tests fail with 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' when POSTing StatefulSet, Deployment, DaemonSet, ReplicaSet, ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim, and Endpoints objects with Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf.

Root cause: decode_core_proto_by_kind() in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs has no match arms for these kinds. extract_body() returns raw proto bytes, which Object::from_bytes() then fails to parse as JSON.

Fix: add prost struct definitions (following field numbers from k8s.io/api/<group>/v1/generated.proto), decode functions, and dispatch entries for each missing kind. Follow the exact pattern of decode_service_proto / decode_cronjob_proto.

Priority kinds (tested by conformance):
- StatefulSet (apps/v1, generated.proto)
- Deployment (apps/v1)
- DaemonSet (apps/v1)
- ReplicaSet (apps/v1)
- ServiceAccount (core/v1)
- PersistentVolumeClaim (core/v1)
- Endpoints (core/v1)

Each needs: struct defs, decode_X_proto fn, dispatch entry in decode_core_proto_by_kind, and at minimum one round-trip unit test.

File to edit: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs
Pattern to follow: decode_cronjob_proto (line 2206) and Service decoder (line 1352).
close_reason: PR #281 opened: adds decode_statefulset_proto, decode_deployment_proto, decode_daemonset_proto, decode_replicaset_proto, decode_serviceaccount_proto, decode_persistentvolumeclaim_proto, decode_endpoints_proto — all wired into decode_core_proto_by_kind; 7 new tests, 1054 total pass

title: fix(sonobuoy): retrieve fails with EOF — results not retrievable from aggregator
description:
sonobuoy retrieve fails with 'error retrieving results: EOF' when run against our apiserver.

Observed:
  KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig sonobuoy retrieve
  error retrieving results: EOF

sonobuoy retrieve works by connecting to the sonobuoy aggregator pod via a port-forward or the aggregator's HTTP endpoint and downloading a tarball of results. EOF means the connection is established but the response body is empty or the connection is closed before the body is sent.

Most likely causes (in order of probability):
1. The sonobuoy aggregator reads results back from the apiserver via a ConfigMap or similar resource — if that retrieval fails or returns unexpected data, the aggregator's HTTP server returns an empty body.
2. The aggregator pod's HTTP handler has a bug triggered by our apiserver's response format for some resource it queries at retrieve-time.
3. Our apiserver drops the connection prematurely on a large response (results tarball can be tens of MB).

Investigation: run sonobuoy with --log-level=debug or check aggregator logs at retrieve time. Compare what endpoint sonobuoy retrieve actually calls (likely a direct pod port-forward to port 8080 on the sonobuoy pod, not through our apiserver). If it's a direct pod connection the EOF is in the aggregator process itself, not our apiserver — check aggregator logs for what it's doing when retrieve is called.

This blocks getting structured pass/fail counts from conformance runs; currently we rely on grepping the e2e job pod logs directly.
close_reason: PR #287 opened — splice deadlock fixed via BiStream split() redesign; regression test added

title: fix(scheduling): pod 'PodScheduled' condition missing from status
description:
2 failures in scheduling/predicates.go:1247 — 'Did not find scheduled condition for pod pfpod'. The test creates a pod and waits for the PodScheduled condition to appear in pod status. Our apiserver stores the pod but never adds the PodScheduled condition.

In a real k8s cluster the scheduler sets this condition. In u7s the kube-scheduler binary runs externally and should be setting it via the pod status subresource. The failure likely means either:
1. The scheduler is not setting the condition (scheduler not running or not connecting)
2. The pod status subresource update is being dropped

Note: the pod JSON seen in the log (builder.go:157) shows conditions include PodReadyToStartContainers/Initialized/Ready/ContainersReady but NOT PodScheduled — suggesting the condition is not being set at any point. The $setElementOrder in the status hints this came from a strategic-merge-patch, which we don't support — so the kubelet status update may itself be failing.

Deferred until strategic-merge-patch (mayor-w5bt) is resolved, as that may be the actual root cause for the missing condition.
notes:
Unblocked: mayor-w5bt (strategic-merge-patch) closed in PR #279. PodScheduled condition can now be investigated.
PR #334: PodScheduled=False initialized on create, set to True in bind_pod; 5 regression tests.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #334 (merged): PodScheduled=False initialized on create; set to True in bind_pod.

title: fix(events): preserve EventSeries and CreationTimestamp on Event PATCH/update
description:
1 failure: core_events.go:144 — after patching an Event to set Series.Count=100 and Series.LastObservedTime, the returned Event has Series=nil and CreationTimestamp={} (zero value) instead of the patched values.

Diff from log:
  - CreationTimestamp: s"2026-05-27 02:24:57 +0000 UTC"
  + CreationTimestamp: v1.Time{}
  - Series: s"&EventSeries{Count:100,LastObservedTime:2017-09-19 13:49:16 +0000 UTC,}"
  + Series: nil

Root cause: the Event PATCH handler (or the JSON serialization round-trip) is dropping the 'series' field and zeroing 'creationTimestamp'. This is likely a missing field in the Event JSON schema stored in the DB — 'series' is an optional nested object (EventSeries with count+lastObservedTime) that may not be in our Object storage path. The creationTimestamp zero is a separate issue: our store may be normalizing empty timestamps.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/instrumentation/core_events.go:144
close_reason: PR #280 opened: fix(events): preserve EventSeries and creationTimestamp through PATCH

title: fix(list): populate continue token in chunked list responses
description:
2 conformance failures in chunking.go: the apiserver does return a continue token for the first page (chunking.go:98 shows 'Retrieved 17/17 results with rv 5925 and continue L3Jl...') but the test fails at chunking.go:108 asserting the continue field is not nil. This suggests the continue token is present in the response but not being decoded/populated into the ListMeta.Continue field that the client reads.

Possible causes:
1. The continue token is set in the response JSON but the field name or encoding is wrong, so the k8s client fails to deserialize it.
2. The second-page request (using the continue token) returns all results instead of a partial page, and the final page has a nil continue — but the test expects the last page to have nil, not an intermediate page.

chunking.go:108 assertion: 'Expected <*int64 | 0x0>: nil not to be nil' — this looks like it's asserting on RemainingItemCount, not the continue token itself.

Investigate: read chunking.go:83-120 in the k8s source to understand exactly what the test asserts. The apiserver list handler may need to populate metadata.remainingItemCount in chunked responses.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/chunking.go:108, :160
close_reason: PR #279 opened

title: fix(discovery): add flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 to API group discovery
description:
2 conformance failures: flowcontrol.go:290 and flowcontrol.go:536 both fail with 'expected flowcontrol API group/version, got [...]' — the API groups list returned by /apis does not include flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io. The test checks that the group exists in discovery before doing anything else, so it fails immediately.

Fix: register flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 in the discovery endpoint. The resources under this group (FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration) don't need to be functional — they just need to be listed in /apis and /apis/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1. A stub that returns empty lists is sufficient to unblock these 2 tests.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/flowcontrol.go:290, :536
close_reason: PR #278 opened — flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 registered in discovery

title: infra: worker-isolated apiserver test environment
description:
Workers currently cannot run live HTTP integration tests (kubectl create, sonobuoy) without conflicting with the shared host apiserver and VM kubelet. Need an isolation strategy before dispatching workers that require runtime validation.

Options under evaluation by operator:
1. Port-isolated host stacks (u7s-apiserver on unique port + state-db, no kubelet, HTTP-level validation only)
2. Ephemeral Lima VMs per worker (full isolation, heavy: 5-10 min startup, ~2GB RAM each)
3. Hybrid: cargo tests in workers, mayor holds the single sonobuoy slot
4. kubernetes-in-docker (requires containerizing u7s, significant infra lift)

Blocked on operator decision. Do not dispatch until decided.

title: feat(patch): support application/strategic-merge-patch+json on namespace and core resources
description:
4 conformance failures from PATCH requests with Content-Type: application/strategic-merge-patch+json. Currently the apiserver returns 415 UnsupportedMediaType. The e2e webhook tests label namespaces using strategic merge patch.

Observed failure: 'error labeling namespace webhook-7006: unsupported media type application/strategic-merge-patch+json; use application/merge-patch+json'
File: test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go:2415

For many core types (Namespace, Pod, etc.), strategic-merge-patch degenerates to merge-patch behaviour — the strategic merge directives (replace/merge list keys) are only relevant for arrays, and most label/annotation patches don't use arrays. A pragmatic approach: accept strategic-merge-patch and apply it as merge-patch (RFC 7386) for now. This closes the conformance gap without requiring a full strategic merge implementation.

Deferred from prior sessions as complexity was unclear. Now confirmed as 4 distinct test failures.
close_reason: PR #279 opened

title: Add kubelet-reconnect script for iterate-on-apiserver workflow
description:
When iterating on the apiserver (cargo build --release && scripts/u7s-start.sh --reset), the developer needs to reconnect the kubelet to the new apiserver CA without re-provisioning the VM. Currently this requires running scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh which is long, mixes first-time provisioning with reconnect, and is not obviously safe to re-run.

Fix:
1. Add scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh — does ONLY: copy kubeconfig (rewritten for host.lima.internal), copy CA cert, write kubelet drop-in, systemctl daemon-reload + restart kubelet, wait for node to appear. No VM provisioning, no iptables, no sonobuoy. ~30 lines.

2. Update the 'next steps' block in scripts/u7s-start.sh to print two clear paths:
   - First run (VM not yet provisioned): scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh
   - Subsequent runs (VM exists): scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh

3. Add a comment at the top of scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh: 'For day-to-day iteration after initial provisioning, use scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh instead.'

Files to modify: scripts/u7s-start.sh, scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh
Files to create: scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh

The iptables DNAT rule (10.96.0.1 → host.lima.internal) survives VM restarts only if the VM was stopped cleanly; on a running VM it persists in memory. kubelet-reconnect.sh should re-apply it idempotently (same as lima-start.sh already does: delete+add).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #274 — scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh added

title: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions — delete or use the dead code
description:
Three dead_code suppressions need real fixes (not allow hacks):

1. crates/apiserver/src/rbac.rs:44 — AggregationRule struct and ClusterRole.aggregation_rule field are marked dead_code. controller-manager/src/lib.rs has its own copy. Either wire aggregation_rule into the apiserver RBAC evaluator (correct fix: aggregate ClusterRoles before policy eval) or delete the struct and field from rbac.rs since the apiserver never uses it.

2. crates/apiserver/src/types.rs:222 — ResourceMeta.namespaced field is set on construction but never read at runtime (routing is done at the axum router level). Either use it (e.g. assert at registration time that cluster-scoped resources are not registered under namespaced routes) or delete the field entirely.

3. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs:16 — PatchQueryParams.field_validation has #[allow(dead_code)] but the field IS constructed in tests (resource.rs:1905,1979) and parsed from the query string. The allow is wrong — check if removing it silences the warning without the allow (the field may not be dead at all, just not read after deserialization because it is intentionally ignored). If dead: document the ignore with a comment on the struct; if not dead: remove the allow.

Each fix must not regress existing tests. File follow-on beads for any new work discovered.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #276

title: Improve kubectl table columns for non-pod resources
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/table.rs build_table() routes to build_generic_table() for everything except pods, returning only Name+Age. Real kubectl -o wide shows resource-specific columns for all common types. Add typed table builders for at least: Nodes (STATUS, ROLES, AGE, VERSION, INTERNAL-IP, EXTERNAL-IP, OS-IMAGE, KERNEL-VERSION, CONTAINER-RUNTIME for wide), Deployments (READY, UP-TO-DATE, AVAILABLE, AGE), Services (TYPE, CLUSTER-IP, EXTERNAL-IP, PORT(S), AGE), ReplicaSets (DESIRED, CURRENT, READY, AGE), StatefulSets (READY, AGE), DaemonSets (DESIRED, CURRENT, READY, UP-TO-DATE, AVAILABLE, AGE), Namespaces (STATUS, AGE), ConfigMaps (DATA, AGE), Secrets (TYPE, DATA, AGE), ServiceAccounts (SECRETS, AGE). Pattern: add a branch in build_table() per (group, plural) pair, same pattern as the existing pod branch. Tests: assert column names and representative cell values for each new type. File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/table.rs only.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #275

title: Add SubjectAccessReview protobuf decoder for kubelet webhook authorization
description: Kubelet sends SubjectAccessReview as protobuf to /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews. No decoder exists; extract_body returns raw bytes to serde_json which fails with 'expected value at line 1 column 1'. Kubelet sees auth denial, returns InternalError to kubectl. Fix: add decode_subject_access_review_proto in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs, register in decode_core_proto_by_kind. Also add TokenReview decoder (same issue for authentication webhook). Tests: wire-level proto decode tests for both types. Ref: .claude/plans/the-real-fix-here-peppy-thimble.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #272 — SubjectAccessReview and TokenReview protobuf decoders merged to main (f0dbc02)

title: batch/v1 proto body decoding: CronJob POST returns 400 from e2e pod
description:
The e2e CronJob conformance test fails because the Go client sends CronJob objects as Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf. Our extract_body() only decodes core/v1 proto types. batch/v1 types (CronJob, Job) have no decoder and the raw proto bytes are returned to Object::from_bytes() which fails with 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'. This is a per-test failure (not a panic), but it will cause many conformance tests to fail once the chunking panic is fixed.

Possible fix approaches:
A) Add batch/v1 proto decoders (CronJob, Job) using prost with batch API proto definitions
B) Return 415 Unsupported Media Type with Accept-Post: application/json when we can't decode a proto body, so clients retry with JSON (most correct but requires client cooperation)
C) Teach the fallback to accept content-type:application/json in the sub-envelope even when outer is proto
close_reason: Fixed in PR #271 — batch/v1 CronJob and Job protobuf decoders merged to main (109a6b4)

title: sonobuoy retrieve: capture results tarball before aggregator pod exits
description: sonobuoy run-all.sh completes but sonobuoy retrieve gets EOF because the aggregator pod has already exited by the time retrieve runs. The tarball exists (sonobuoy status --json shows tar-info) but the HTTP endpoint on the pod is gone. Alternative: copy the tarball out of the pod volume before the pod terminates (kubectl cp sonobuoy/sonobuoy:/tmp/sonobuoy /local/path). The duplicate-aggregator-pod warning is also a symptom: --reset must fully drain the sonobuoy namespace (wait for Terminating→gone) before starting a new run, otherwise the old aggregator pod is still visible when sonobuoy create runs.

title: kubectl logs fails: apiserver cannot proxy kubelet log requests (401 Unauthorized)
description: kubectl logs <pod> fails with 'kubelet request failed: error sending request for url (https://<node-ip>:10250/containerLogs/...)'. The apiserver proxies log requests to kubelet at port 10250. Kubelet responds 401 Unauthorized because the apiserver is not presenting a valid client certificate that kubelet trusts for log access. In real kube-apiserver, log proxying uses the apiserver's kubelet client cert (a separate cert signed by the cluster CA that kubelet accepts). u7s does not have a kubelet client cert configuration — it either does not present a cert, or presents one kubelet does not trust. This blocks: kubectl logs, kubectl exec, kubectl port-forward (all go through the same proxy path). Lower priority than fieldValidation bug since sonobuoy conformance tests do not require kubectl logs to pass.
close_reason: kubelet client cert fix landed in PR #258: proxy requests now present client cert, resolving kubelet auth rejection

title: CIDR-based clusterIP auto-allocation for Services
description:
When a Service is created without spec.clusterIP (or with spec.clusterIP=""), the apiserver should auto-allocate an IP from a configured CIDR range (--service-cluster-ip-range, e.g. 10.96.0.0/12). Currently u7s stores whatever the caller provides with no allocation.

Design: use the existing SQLite store's CAS uniqueness guarantee rather than a new table or in-memory bitmap.

Allocation protocol:
1. Parse the CIDR range at startup; iterate candidate IPs (skip network address, skip first IP reserved for kubernetes/default svc, skip broadcast).
2. To claim IP X: attempt store.put_sync('/registry/service-ips/X', sentinel, create_only=true). The objects table has UNIQUE on key — if another writer claimed X concurrently, the CAS fails. Retry with next candidate.
3. On Service DELETE: store.delete('/registry/service-ips/<clusterIP>') to release.
4. On startup: scan /registry/service-ips/* to reconstruct in-memory 'known allocated' set for fast iteration (avoid always starting from .1).

std::net::Ipv4Addr arithmetic suffices for iteration — no external CIDR crate needed. u32::from(Ipv4Addr) + 1 walks the range.

Config: add --service-cluster-ip-range flag (default 10.96.0.0/12 matching kubeadm) to main.rs. Pass into AppState.

Scope: crates/apiserver/src/main.rs (flag), crates/apiserver/src/state.rs (allocator field), crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs (wire into apply_defaults for Services on create). The apply_defaults function already runs at every write path.

Note: headless services (clusterIP='None') skip allocation. ExternalName services skip allocation. Only ClusterIP-type services need it.
close_reason: Merged as PR #243 (6cf619f). CIDR-based clusterIP auto-allocation via CAS on /registry/service-ips/ sentinels. --service-cluster-ip-range flag, ServiceIpAllocator in state.rs, maybe_allocate_cluster_ip in create path, release on DELETE. 6 new unit tests.

title: feat(conformance): add reset.sh — full teardown + clean VM recreate for fresh conformance runs
description:
Before each sonobuoy run we need a guaranteed clean slate. The current conformance stack has no teardown step. Stale state causes: ghost node registrations, stale CSRs, kubelet reconnecting with certs that don't match a regenerated CA, leftover pod sandboxes in the VM.

What to build: scripts/conformance/reset.sh (and wire into run-all.sh as step 00, or make it a standalone prerequisite):

1. Kill host processes:
   - Read PID from temp/u7s/apiserver.pid and temp/u7s/scheduler.pid if they exist; kill -0 to check, then kill
   - Fallback: pkill -f u7s-apiserver; pkill -f u7s-scheduler
   - Remove temp/u7s/ entirely (wipes DB, certs, kubeconfig, PID files)

2. Clean up VM processes (if lima-node VM exists):
   - limactl shell lima-node pkill -f kubelet || true
   - limactl shell lima-node pkill -f kube-controller-manager || true
   - limactl shell lima-node pkill -f sonobuoy || true

3. Delete and recreate the VM:
   - limactl delete --force lima-node
   - This destroys the disk entirely — no stale node state, no stale certs, no leftover containers
   - The next run of 03-start-lima.sh recreates it from the provision script

4. Do NOT recreate the VM here — that is 03-start-lima.sh's job. reset.sh just destroys.

run-all.sh should NOT call reset.sh automatically — a reset takes time (VM recreate is ~2 min) and the operator may want to reuse a running stack for targeted reruns (--focus). Instead: document that reset.sh should be run before a fresh conformance run, and add a --reset flag to run-all.sh that calls it if requested.

Verify with mcp__lima-node__run_shell_command:
- After reset.sh runs: limactl list should show lima-node as nonexistent or in 'Stopped' state before delete completes
- pgrep -f u7s-apiserver and pgrep -f u7s-scheduler should return nothing on the host
- temp/u7s/ should not exist
close_reason: Closed

title: feat(conformance): add 05-start-scheduler.sh to local sonobuoy stack
description:
scripts/conformance/ runs: 01-build → 02-start-apiserver → 03-start-lima → 04-start-kcm → 05-run-sonobuoy. There is no scheduler step, so any sonobuoy Pod without spec.nodeName stays Pending forever. This blocks all sonobuoy conformance testing.

What to add:
- scripts/conformance/05-start-scheduler.sh — start u7s-scheduler inside the lima VM (same pattern as 04-start-kcm.sh: limactl shell lima-node nohup ...). The scheduler binary must be built for linux/arm64 (lima VM arch) and either cross-compiled or built inside the VM. The repo is mounted read-only in the VM at the host path, so the binary cannot be written there — write to /tmp/ inside the VM.
- Renumber the sonobuoy script: 05-run-sonobuoy.sh → 06-run-sonobuoy.sh. Update run-all.sh to call the new name.
- scripts/conformance/run-all.sh must call 05-start-scheduler.sh before 06-run-sonobuoy.sh.

The scheduler uses the same kubeconfig as kcm-start.sh (cert-based, host.lima.internal rewrite already in kcm-start.sh — apply same pattern for scheduler). The scheduler binary takes --kubeconfig flag.

Build approach: the simplest path that avoids cross-compilation is to build u7s-scheduler inside the lima VM (cargo is available there via the provisioning script). Check scripts/lima-start.sh to see what's installed. If cargo is not available in the VM, fall back to cross-compiling on the host (cross crate or cargo-zigbuild). Pick whichever is simpler; document the choice in a comment.

Verify by running scripts/conformance/run-all.sh through step 05 (scheduler start) and confirming the scheduler process is alive inside the VM before handing off.

title: feat(bench): include u7s-scheduler in RSS idle and load benchmarks
description:
The bench-rss.sh (idle), bench-rss-load.sh (load), and the perf.yaml bench-rss-deploy job currently measure apiserver+kcm only. The scheduler is now a first-class component and its footprint must be included in all three measurements.

What to change:
1. scripts/bench-rss.sh — after apiserver starts, also build+start u7s-scheduler (cargo build --release -p u7s-scheduler, then ./target/release/u7s-scheduler --kubeconfig $TMPDIR/kubeconfig). Measure sum of apiserver+scheduler RSS against the 64 MB threshold. Update threshold comment.
2. scripts/bench-rss-load.sh — same pattern: start scheduler alongside apiserver. It does not need to do any scheduling work during the load bench; just must be running so its idle RSS is counted.
3. perf.yaml bench-rss-deploy job — this job already starts kcm alongside apiserver. Also start u7s-scheduler binary (built from the repo, not downloaded). Sample combined RSS of apiserver+kcm+scheduler. The 10 MB delta threshold on this job measures growth, not idle, so no threshold change needed there — but the baseline must include scheduler.

The scheduler connects to apiserver via the kubeconfig written at startup. It needs the cert-based kubeconfig (not the token one) since it uses mTLS. In bench-rss-deploy, kubeconfig-cert is already saved before token kubeconfig overwrites it — use that.

Do NOT change the 64 MB idle threshold yet — first measure, then we will know if it needs adjusting. Report actual measured RSS values in the PR description so we can decide.

title: research: effort estimate for proper OpenAPI spec + protobuf encoding
description:
Audit the current state of OpenAPI and protobuf support in u7s and estimate the effort to make them production-grade.

**OpenAPI:**
u7s currently serves an OpenAPI spec (enough for kubectl to work) but it is likely hand-maintained or partially generated. Questions to answer:
- What does u7s currently serve at /openapi/v2 and /openapi/v3?
- How does it compare to the real kube OpenAPI spec (missing endpoints, wrong schemas, missing CRD schemas)?
- What would it cost to generate it properly (e.g. from code annotations or by embedding the upstream spec)?
- What conformance gates depend on a correct OpenAPI spec (kubectl --validate, sonobuoy, Argo CD drift detection)?

**Protobuf:**
u7s has proto.rs infrastructure but currently returns JSON for all requests regardless of Accept header. Kubelet 1.36 sends Accept: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf. Questions to answer:
- What is the current proto.rs scope — which types are covered?
- Which clients/controllers actually require protobuf (kubelet? kcm? kubectl?)?
- What is the decoding path cost — do we need to maintain proto definitions or can we transcode JSON→protobuf at response time?
- Rough LoC estimate and risk for each approach.

**Output:** a findings doc at ai/findings/openapi-protobuf-research-YYYY-MM-DD.md covering current state, gaps, effort estimates (S/M/L/XL), and a recommendation on sequencing. File any actionable follow-on beads as part of the research.

Argo CD health assessment reads deployment.status.availableReplicas to determine Healthy state. Without a deployment controller, all Deployments stay Progressing/Degraded forever and Argo CD never marks apps Synced+Healthy.

title: feat(namespaces): implement finalizer-based deletion lifecycle
description:
delete_namespace currently hard-deletes the namespace immediately. Real Kubernetes sets deletionTimestamp and phase=Terminating, then a namespace controller drains all child resources before removing the finalizer.

Argo CD uses CreateNamespace=true sync option and watches namespace deletion for app lifecycle tracking. Instant deletion without Terminating phase breaks its GC logic and can cause stale object collisions on re-create.

Fix: (1) apiserver: on DELETE, set deletionTimestamp+phase=Terminating instead of hard-delete when finalizers present; seed kubernetes finalizer on namespace create. (2) u7s-controller-manager: watch namespaces in Terminating phase, drain child resources, patch to remove finalizer.

System namespaces seeded with kubernetes finalizer. New namespace_controller in u7s-controller-manager: watches namespaces, adds kubernetes finalizer on ADDED, drains core resources and removes finalizer on MODIFIED+Terminating.

title: feat(ssa): return managedFields in apply-patch+yaml responses
description:
Argo CD uses --server-side apply. u7s remaps application/apply-patch+yaml to StrategicMerge (acknowledged in json_patch.rs). No managedFields are tracked or returned. Argo CD's client library uses managedFields to determine field ownership; without it Argo CD reports all resources as OutOfSync causing infinite reconcile loops.

Minimum viable fix: strip incoming managedFields from the apply body, then echo back a synthetic managedFields block [{manager: <fieldManager param>, operation: Apply, apiVersion, time}] in the response. Full conflict detection (HTTP 409 on field ownership conflict) is a stretch goal.

title: fix(discovery): add missing shortNames for built-in resources
description:
## Summary
The discovery endpoint (handlers/discovery.rs) is missing shortNames in two places:

1. Static built-in resource entries — most resources have no shortNames array
2. Dynamic CRD entries (lines 203-210) — the .map() block omits 'shortNames' even though crd.spec.names.short_names is already deserialized

kubectl resolves short names by reading shortNames from APIResourceList discovery response — the server never sees the short name. Without these entries, commands like 'kubectl get rs' fail with 'the server doesn't have a resource type rs'. Same applies to any CRD with shortNames in its spec.

## Fix part 1: Static resources missing shortNames (upstream canonical values)
- replicasets: rs
- deployments: deploy
- daemonsets: ds
- statefulsets: sts
- pods: po
- services: svc
- endpoints: ep
- namespaces: ns
- nodes: no
- configmaps: cm
- persistentvolumes: pv
- persistentvolumeclaims: pvc
- serviceaccounts: sa
- resourcequotas: quota
- limitranges: limits
- ingresses: ing
- networkpolicies: netpol
- poddisruptionbudgets: pdb
- storageclasses: sc
(hpa, cj, csr, crd already have shortNames)

## Fix part 2: Dynamic CRD discovery (discovery.rs ~line 204)
Add 'shortNames': crd.spec.names.short_names to the serde_json::json! block in the .map() closure. The field is already deserialized as Vec<String> on CrdNames.

## Test
- Unit test: static discovery response contains shortNames for a representative set
- Unit test: CRD installed with shortNames appears in its group's APIResourceList with those shortNames forwarded
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: CI smoke workflow interpolates matrix.k8s directly into shell — latent injection
description:
## Summary

In `.github/workflows/smoke.yaml` (lines 49, 55, 262, 305, 311, 514, 574) the
`matrix.k8s` expression is interpolated directly into `run:` shell blocks using
`${{ matrix.k8s }}`:

```yaml
MINOR=$(echo "${{ matrix.k8s }}" | cut -d. -f1-2)
sudo apt-get install -y --allow-downgrades "kubectl=${{ matrix.k8s }}-*"
```

## Impact

Currently not exploitable: the matrix is a hardcoded static list. However, this
interpolation pattern is a latent command injection vulnerability. If the matrix
value source ever changes (e.g. via a workflow_dispatch input or PR label), an
attacker could inject arbitrary shell commands executed on the CI runner, which has
access to GitHub Actions secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, repository credentials, etc.).

GitHub's own security hardening guide explicitly calls this pattern out as dangerous.

## Location

- `.github/workflows/smoke.yaml:49,55,262,305,311,514,574`

## Fix

Assign matrix.k8s to an environment variable at the step level and use the env
variable in the shell body:

```yaml
env:
  K8S_VERSION: ${{ matrix.k8s }}
run: |
  MINOR=$(echo "$K8S_VERSION" | cut -d. -f1-2)
  sudo apt-get install -y --allow-downgrades "kubectl=${K8S_VERSION}-*"
```

Apply consistently across all three jobs (kubectl, kubelet, kcm) in the workflow.
close_reason: PR #183 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/183

title: fix: try_verify_client_cert does not verify cert chain against cluster CA
description:
## Summary

`try_verify_client_cert` (auth.rs:213) parses DER bytes and extracts CN/O fields
without itself performing any chain validation. Chain validation is delegated to
rustls (via WebPkiClientVerifier). However, the function name implies verification
but it only extracts identity, creating a misleading contract.

## Specific Risks

1. The function can be called with arbitrary DER bytes by any caller, yielding a
   UserInfo with no chain validation performed at that layer.
2. If `cluster_ca_der` is None at startup (e.g. CA load failure), the
   WebPkiClientVerifier trust store is empty. Rustls may reject all client certs
   at the TLS layer, but the error path is not audited for whether the cert extension
   is silently propagated.
3. The misleading name makes future callers likely to bypass chain validation.

## Location

- `crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:213–258` (try_verify_client_cert)
- `crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:311–315` (WebPkiClientVerifier construction)

## Fix

Rename to `extract_client_cert_identity`. Add a startup check that panics or
returns an error if `cluster_ca_der` is None, so the trust store is never empty.
Add a code comment at the call site making clear that rustls has already verified
the chain.
close_reason: PR #184 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/184

title: fix: remove hardcoded system:masters bypass in ClusterRoleBinding escalation check
description:
## Summary

`check_crb_escalation` (handlers/generic.rs:316–318) has a hardcoded bypass that
unconditionally allows system:masters to create any ClusterRoleBinding:

```rust
if user.groups.iter().any(|g| g == "system:masters") {
    return Ok(());
}
```

## Impact

This is inconsistent with the project's design principle that all system:masters
privilege flows through RBAC data (the seeded `cluster-admin` ClusterRole and
`system:masters` ClusterRoleBinding), not through hardcoded logic. The RBAC tests
(`rbac.rs:459`) explicitly assert that system:masters must be denied when no binding
exists. This bypass undermines that invariant.

If the seeded binding is deleted or corrupted, the code still grants escalation.
Conversely, any other group granted cluster-admin via RBAC (not literally named
system:masters) is still subject to the check, creating asymmetric behaviour.

## Location

- `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:316–318`

## Fix

Remove the system:masters special-case. The `user_holds_all_rules` check will
correctly handle system:masters members (via the seeded cluster-admin binding) because
`is_allowed` returns true for all wildcard-rule requests. This makes privilege
entirely data-driven.
close_reason: PR #185 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/185

title: test: call_conversion_webhook error paths unverified (Failure response, empty convertedObjects)

title: feat(api): implement certificates.k8s.io/v1 CSR API surface — CertificateSigningRequest CRUD + status.certificate write-back
description:
feat(api): implement certificates.k8s.io/v1 CSR API surface — CertificateSigningRequest CRUD + /status + /approval subresources

## Scope

Cluster-scoped resource. Three surfaces:

1. Registry + discovery: add certificates.k8s.io/v1 group, CertificateSigningRequest resource metadata (~20 lines).
2. /status subresource: handled generically by existing handlers/status.rs — zero new handler code.
3. /approval subresource (NEW — required for kubectl/kube-controller-manager compat):
   - kubectl certificate approve/deny uses PATCH/PUT /approval exclusively
   - kube-controller-manager signing controller sets status.conditions via /approval
   - Must write only status.conditions; must not touch status.certificate
   - ~40-60 lines in a dedicated handler

## Types

CertificateSigningRequestSpec and Status serde structs inline in crates/apiserver/src/types/, following existing pattern.

## Validation (strict — security-critical path)

Dedicated CSR POST handler (not pure generic passthrough):
- spec.request: required, must be valid base64, decoded bytes must be valid DER-encoded PKCS#10 CSR
- spec.signerName: required, non-empty string
- Return 422 Unprocessable Entity on any violation

Validation must be thoroughly tested — this is a security-critical codepath.

## Tests (required per Rule 14)

Rejection paths:
1. POST with missing spec.request → 422
2. POST with invalid base64 in spec.request → 422
3. POST with valid base64 but invalid PKCS#10 DER in spec.request → 422
4. POST with missing spec.signerName → 422
5. PUT /approval with status.conditions[].type=Denied — assert status.certificate is never written
6. OCC conflict on /status write — PUT with stale resourceVersion → 409
7. RBAC rejection (if RBAC enforced at handler level)

Happy path:
- Full lifecycle: POST → GET → PUT /approval (Approved) → PUT /status (certificate write-back) → GET confirms status.certificate present

## Out of scope for this bead

- Full OpenAPI schema validation / admission webhooks (future)
- spec.request validation beyond base64 + valid PKCS#10 DER (e.g. SANs, key type enforcement)
- /approval subresource RBAC isolation (certificatesigningrequests/approval verb) — future

## Architectural note (recorded 2026-05-22)

Bead note 'generic handler is sufficient' was incorrect. /approval is mandatory for kubectl certificate approve/deny and kube-controller-manager CSR approval flow. /status is already generic. /approval is new dedicated handler.
notes: Testing must cover rejection paths — CSR security role is critical. Required rejection test cases: (1) POST with invalid/missing spec.request (malformed PEM), (2) approval denied — PUT approval with status.conditions[].type=Denied, assert cert is never written back, (3) RBAC rejection — request without necessary group/verb permissions (if RBAC enforced), (4) OCC conflict on status write — PUT status with stale resourceVersion returns 409. Operator note 2026-05-22: generic handler is sufficient for now; full spec compliance is a future goal; testing strategy clarified including rejection coverage.

Without a seeded ClusterRoleBinding mapping system:nodes group to the system:node ClusterRole, kubelets using node credentials (not system:masters bypass) cannot create leases, post events, update node status, or read their pods. Fix: at apiserver startup, ensure a ClusterRoleBinding exists binding the system:nodes group to the system:node ClusterRole (same pattern as the existing system:masters seeding). This unblocks local development with properly-credentialed kubelets (not system:masters bypass) and is a prerequisite for correct CSR bootstrap flow.

title: fix(deps): jsonwebtoken v10 requires CryptoProvider::install_default() in tests
description: Renovate PR #117 upgrades jsonwebtoken 8.x→10.x. jsonwebtoken-10 changed the crypto backend to require explicit CryptoProvider selection at runtime. 5 tests in auth.rs panic: 'Could not automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider from jsonwebtoken crate features. Call CryptoProvider::install_default() before this point.' Fix: add CryptoProvider::install_default() call in each affected test (or a test setup function). Tests: test_authn_expired_sa_jwt_rejected, test_authn_sa_jwt_wrong_key_rejected, test_authn_tampered_sa_jwt_rejected, test_authn_valid_sa_jwt_authenticates, test_sa_jwt_namespace_scoped_group. After fix, PR #117 should go green and can be merged.

title: feat(apiserver): implement storage.k8s.io/v1 CSINode and CSIDriver endpoints
description:
Kubelet tries to PATCH /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csinodes/{name} to set a NodeID annotation as part of CSI initialization. The server returns 404 (storage.k8s.io is not a registered API group), causing client-go to emit 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' and the kubelet to never reach Ready=True.

## What to implement

Register routes for:
- GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csinodes
- GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csinodes/{name}
- GET/LIST/WATCH /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csidrivers
- GET/LIST/WATCH /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csidrivers/{name}

CSINode and CSIDriver are cluster-scoped resources. Use the existing generic_handler infrastructure from main.rs (same as nodes, namespaces, etc.). No status subresource needed for basic kubelet compat.

Also register discovery:
- GET /apis/storage.k8s.io → APIGroup response
- GET /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1 → APIResourceList with csinodes and csidrivers

## Success criteria

After this PR, 'Assert node reaches Ready' in the kubelet smoke test should pass. Verify by checking that a CSINode object is created in the store when the kubelet initializes.
close_reason: PR #120 opened: adds CSINode create/get round-trip test; all storage.k8s.io infrastructure was already in place

title: CodeQL: add permissions blocks to workflow jobs (actions/missing-workflow-permissions)
description:
CodeQL rule actions/missing-workflow-permissions flagged 9 jobs that do not declare a permissions block. Affected: smoke.yaml jobs at lines 11, 209; test.yaml jobs at lines 8, 20, 32, 44; perf.yaml jobs at lines 11, 28.

Fix: add 'permissions: {}' (deny-all) or a minimal explicit permissions block to each job. For jobs that only read code, 'permissions: contents: read' is appropriate. Resolves CodeQL alerts 1-8.

title: CodeQL: pin GitHub Actions to commit SHA (actions/unpinned-tag)
description:
CodeQL rule actions/unpinned-tag flagged 17 workflow steps using mutable version tags (e.g. actions/checkout@v4) instead of pinned commit SHAs. Affected files: smoke.yaml, test.yaml, perf.yaml, coverage-baseline.yaml.

Fix: replace all uses-tag references with uses: action@<sha> using the current SHA for each action version. This prevents supply chain attacks where a tag is moved to a malicious commit. Use 'gh api /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/tags/{tag}' or the GitHub Actions pinning convention. Resolves CodeQL alerts 9-26.

title: CodeQL: path injection in tls.rs and auth.rs (rust/path-injection)
description:
CodeQL rule rust/path-injection flagged 8 locations where CLI args flow into filesystem paths without validation.

tls.rs lines: 389, 565, 589, 599, 613, 623
auth.rs lines: 68, 678

These are paths supplied via CLI flags (--tls-cert, --sa-key, --token-auth-file, etc.) passed to std::fs::read/write. Fix: add a helper that validates each path is a non-traversal absolute path, call it on every CLI-supplied path before fs::read/write. Add a test for the validation logic. Resolves CodeQL alerts 27-34.
