title: security: CRD group name can shadow built-in API groups
description: In handlers/crd.rs:create_crd(), there is no validation that the CRD's spec.group does not overlap with built-in API groups (e.g., apps, rbac.authorization.k8s.io, authorization.k8s.io). A user with CRD create permissions could register a CRD with group='rbac.authorization.k8s.io' and plural='clusterroles', potentially shadowing or interfering with built-in RBAC endpoints. While route ordering means specific routes (like authorization endpoints) take priority, the generic catch-all routes for /apis/{group}/{version}/{resource} would serve the CRD's custom resources, creating confusion and potential security issues.
close_reason: PR #107 opened: validate_crd_group() blocks 19 built-in groups with 422 in crd.rs

title: security: no namespace/name path traversal validation on generic handlers
description: The generic handlers in handlers/generic.rs accept namespace and name path parameters from the URL without validating them against path traversal characters. While Namespace::parse() validates namespace names on dedicated namespace endpoints (only [a-z0-9-]+), the generic handler's Path((group, version, ns, resource, name)) parameters are used directly in keys::group_object_key() without validation. Crafted namespace or name values containing '/' could construct store keys that access objects in other namespaces or resource types. Example: PUT /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/../../secrets/default/target would construct a key that crosses namespace boundaries.
close_reason: PR #107 opened: validate_name() in generic.rs, called from all ns/name handlers

title: security: SubjectAccessReview does not require elevated privileges
description: In handlers/authorization.rs, subject_access_review() does not use the Extension(user) and does not check the caller's identity. Any authenticated user (or anonymous, if RBAC allows it) can query SubjectAccessReview to probe whether arbitrary users have access to arbitrary resources. In real Kubernetes, SubjectAccessReview requires system:auth-delegator or equivalent permissions. Here, the standard auth middleware gate applies the verb 'create' on 'subjectaccessreviews', but the seed RBAC doesn't restrict it, allowing any user with wide create permissions to probe the RBAC state of other users.
close_reason: PR #106 opened: in-handler privilege check added to subject_access_review with 4 unit tests; middleware gate (Option 1) already in place, handler check is defense-in-depth

title: security: SA key file written with no explicit permission restriction (world-readable)
description: In tls.rs:load_or_generate_sa_keys(), std::fs::write(sa_key_path, ...) writes the RSA private key to disk using default file permissions (typically 0o644 on Unix). This means the SA signing key is world-readable. Any local process can read the key and mint valid service-account JWTs, gaining cluster-admin equivalent access for any ServiceAccount. The CA key is written the same way. Both keys must be written with 0o600 (owner-only) permissions.
close_reason: PR #107 opened: write_private_key() with mode 0o600 in tls.rs

title: security: RBAC index does not prevent privilege escalation via ClusterRoleBinding self-grant
description: When a user has create/update permission on clusterrolebindings (rbac.authorization.k8s.io), they can create a ClusterRoleBinding that binds themselves to the cluster-admin ClusterRole. The RBAC engine in rbac.rs applies the binding immediately via apply_object without any escalation check. Kubernetes real RBAC prevents this by requiring the caller to already hold every permission in the referenced role. This is a privilege escalation path: any user who can write ClusterRoleBindings can grant themselves cluster-admin.
close_reason: PR #106 opened: user_holds_all_rules + cluster_role_rules added to rbac.rs with 3 escalation-prevention unit tests

title: watch: parse and honour allowWatchBookmarks query parameter
description:
LOW severity conformance gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

CollectionQuery in generic.rs does not include allowWatchBookmarks. The server currently sends periodic BOOKMARK events unconditionally (every 60s and on stream close), regardless of whether the client opted in via ?allowWatchBookmarks=true.

Per the Kubernetes watch protocol, BOOKMARK events should only be sent when the client explicitly requests them. Sending them unconditionally is safe (client-go ignores unexpected bookmarks), but:
1. It wastes bandwidth for clients that did not opt in.
2. It is a conformance deviation that could cause issues with non-client-go consumers.

Fix: add allow_watch_bookmarks: Option<bool> to CollectionQuery; thread the flag through to watch_generic and watch_pods; suppress periodic bookmark emission when the flag is absent or false. The sendInitialEvents BOOKMARK (with k8s.io/initial-events-end annotation) should still be sent unconditionally when sendInitialEvents=true, as that bookmark signals end-of-initial-list rather than a progress marker.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (CollectionQuery, watch_generic), crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs (watch_pods)

title: watch: return HTTP 410 before streaming when initial resourceVersion is already expired
description:
MED severity gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

When a client opens a fresh watch with ?resourceVersion=N where N is below the compaction horizon, u7s currently:
1. Returns HTTP 200 OK (flushing headers)
2. Immediately emits a WatchEvent::Compacted as a JSON error body: {"type":"ERROR","object":{"code":410,...}}

This matches kube-apiserver behavior AFTER headers are committed mid-stream. However, for a brand-new watch the Kubernetes API spec says the server SHOULD return HTTP 410 (Gone) directly — before sending any body — so clients can detect the failure synchronously rather than needing to parse the NDJSON error body.

The store's watch() function at lib.rs:696 already yields Compacted immediately if from_revision < horizon. The fix is to check the compaction horizon BEFORE calling state.store.watch() and returning the streaming response. If from_revision > 0 && from_revision < horizon, return a proper HTTP 410 Status response instead of entering the stream.

The mid-stream 410 error body path should remain for cases where compaction happens WHILE watching.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (watch_generic or its callers), crates/store/src/lib.rs (expose compaction_horizon check)

title: watch: labelSelector and fieldSelector silently dropped from live watch stream for non-pod resources
description:
HIGH severity gap found in watch audit (mayor-24ig).

In list_resource (generic.rs:510-528) and list_namespaced_resource (generic.rs:958-976), when watch=true the code calls watch_generic() but does NOT pass label_selector or field_selector. These filters are only applied to the initial LIST response.

watch_generic() (generic.rs:219) has no selector parameters at all. Live watch events after the initial list are delivered unfiltered to the client.

By contrast, watch_pods (pods.rs:281) correctly accepts and applies field_selector to live events (pods.rs:378-391).

Impact: client-go watchers using labelSelector or fieldSelector receive ALL events for the resource type. Informer caches may be populated with objects they should not see, causing reconcilers to act on wrong state. For high-volume clusters this also wastes significant CPU/network.

Fix: add label_selector and field_selector parameters to watch_generic(); apply them to each incoming WatchEvent::Added and WatchEvent::Modified before yielding. Deleted events should pass through (client must clean up what it was tracking).

Regression test: watch with labelSelector=app=foo should not receive events for objects with app=bar.

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs (watch_generic, list_resource, list_namespaced_resource)

title: Seed minimal Argo CD RBAC: ClusterRoles and ServiceAccounts needed for Argo CD install
description:
## Goal

When Argo CD installs, it applies a set of ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, and ServiceAccounts. If these fail (e.g. due to RBAC gaps), the install aborts. Seeding the minimum required RBAC at startup (like we do for system:node) would let us test Argo CD install against u7s without needing RBAC to be fully implemented first.

## What to seed

At minimum for Argo CD to start:
- ServiceAccount `argocd-application-controller` in namespace `argocd`
- ServiceAccount `argocd-server` in namespace `argocd`
- ClusterRole `argocd-application-controller` with rules covering apps, deployments, services, configmaps, secrets, pods, etc.
- ClusterRoleBinding linking the above

## Note

This is a workaround bead — once SA token projection (mayor-vacv) and full RBAC work, seeding won't be needed. Mark as deferred until we actually try an Argo CD install and hit this specific gap. For now: **DEFER**.

## Depends on

mayor-vacv (SA token projection)

title: RBAC: enforce api_group on RoleRef and ClusterRoleRef binding resolution
description:
## Goal

Argo CD creates ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings with `roleRef.apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io`. Currently u7s ignores the `api_group` field on RoleRef during RBAC evaluation — it only matches by name. This is a correctness gap that could cause Argo CD's RBAC bindings to match unintended roles if names collide across API groups.

## Current state

`Subject::namespace` and `RoleRef::api_group` are both deserialized but never read (noted in dead code audit). RBAC evaluation in `rbac.rs` does name-only matching.

## Steps

1. In the RBAC evaluator, when resolving a RoleRef, also check that `roleRef.apiGroup` matches the expected group (`rbac.authorization.k8s.io` for ClusterRole/Role, `""` for legacy).
2. Add a test: binding with wrong apiGroup should not grant access.
3. Remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `RoleRef::api_group` once it's wired up (mayor-vm3l covers the annotation removal, but the wiring is the correctness fix here).

## Not blocked by proto fix.

title: CRD status subresource: serve /status subresource endpoint for CRs that declare hasStatusSubresource
description:
## Goal

Argo CD writes `.status` on its own CRDs (Application, AppProject) via the status subresource (`PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status`). Currently u7s serves CRDs without a status subresource — all fields are writable on the main endpoint, which is a conformance gap (noted in architectural memory).

## What's needed

1. When a CRD is created with `spec.versions[].subresources.status: {}`, set `has_status_subresource: true` in the stored `ResourceMeta`.

2. Add route: `PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status` and `PUT /apis/{group}/{version}/namespaces/{ns}/{plural}/{name}/status` — accepts a full object body but only persists the `.status` field, ignoring spec changes.

3. On the main `PUT`/`PATCH` endpoint for resources with a status subresource, strip `.status` from the incoming body before persisting (status can only be written via the `/status` subresource).

4. `GET /apis/{group}/{version}/{plural}/{name}/status` — returns the full object (same as GET on the main endpoint).

## Tests

- Create a CRD with status subresource; create a CR; PUT to `/status` updates `.status`; PUT to main endpoint does not update `.status`.
- Regression: without status subresource, main PUT persists `.status` normally.

## Not blocked by proto fix.
close_reason: PR #114 opened: feat(crd): CRD status subresource (mayor-zcur)

title: Strategic merge patch (SMP) support for CRs: reject with 415 not 400, or implement basic SMP
description:
## Goal

Argo CD uses strategic merge patch when syncing standard Kubernetes resources. For CRs it typically uses server-side apply or merge patch, but the current rejection message and status code for SMP on CRs needs to be correct.

## Current state

`validate_patch_content_type` in `cr.rs` rejects `application/strategic-merge-patch+json` with HTTP 400. The correct code per the Kubernetes API conventions is **415 Unsupported Media Type**. Argo CD may retry or fail hard depending on the status code.

For built-in resources (Deployments, Services, etc. served through generic.rs), SMP may or may not be implemented — needs checking.

## Steps

1. Change the 400 to 415 in `cr.rs` `validate_patch_content_type` for SMP rejection.
2. Check `generic.rs` patch handler — does it handle `application/strategic-merge-patch+json`? If not, add a 415 rejection with the same pattern.
3. Add regression tests for both.

## Note

Full SMP semantics (list merging by strategic keys) are complex and out of scope here. Correct rejection with 415 is sufficient for now — Argo CD will fall back to merge patch.

## Not blocked by proto fix.

title: CI: auto-update coverage threshold after every merge to main
description:
## Goal

After every merge to main, recompute the coverage threshold and update
`--fail-under-lines N` in `.github/workflows/test.yaml` automatically.
This keeps the gate meaningful without manual intervention.

## Design

Add a new GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/coverage-baseline.yaml`:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
```

Steps:
1. `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only --json` — parse line coverage %
2. Compute threshold = floor(coverage - 5)
3. Use `sed` to update the `--fail-under-lines N` value in `.github/workflows/test.yaml`
4. If the value changed, commit and push to main with message:
   `ci(coverage): update threshold to N (was M) [skip ci]`
   The `[skip ci]` prevents infinite loop — GitHub Actions skips workflows
   when the commit message contains `[skip ci]`.

## Implementation notes

- Extract coverage % with `jq`: `.data.totals.lines.percent`
- Use `sed -i` to replace `--fail-under-lines [0-9]*` with `--fail-under-lines N`
- Git identity for the commit: use `github-actions[bot]` (standard pattern)
- Only commit if N differs from current value (avoid no-op commits)
- Needs `contents: write` permission on the workflow job

## Quality gates

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
- Manually verify: push a test commit to main and check the workflow fires
  and updates the value correctly

## Rule 13

Use `jq` + `sed` for JSON extraction and file editing. No Python.

title: CI: enforce per-crate coverage thresholds
description:
## Goal

Establish a coverage gate in `.github/workflows/test.yaml` so CI fails when test coverage drops below a defined threshold. This prevents coverage regressions as the codebase grows.

## Context

PR #89 added a `coverage` job (`cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only`) but with no enforcement — it just measures. Without a threshold, the job is informational only and cannot block regressions.

Industry standard: 80% line coverage is the common gate. Pre-alpha posture: set initial thresholds conservatively (~5% below observed baseline) to avoid flapping gates.

## Steps

1. Check the actual coverage numbers from the first CI run of PR #89 (or run `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only` locally from main) to establish baselines per crate.

2. Set per-crate thresholds (or a workspace-wide threshold initially):
   - `u7s-store`: target 85%+ (pure logic, easily testable)
   - `u7s-apiserver`: target 65%+ (async handlers covered partly by smoke CI)
   - Workspace overall: use observed baseline minus 5%

3. Update `.github/workflows/test.yaml` `coverage` job to use `--fail-under <N>` (or equivalent llvm-cov flag) so the job exits non-zero when coverage drops below threshold.

4. Commit with a regression test: add a trivial uncovered function to verify the gate fires, then remove it.

5. If `cargo llvm-cov` does not support `--fail-under` directly, use `--json` output + `jq` to extract the totals line and assert `>= N`.

## Quality gates

- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- CI coverage job must exit non-zero on a deliberately-uncovered branch

## Notes

- Do NOT set global threshold before measuring — ground the gate in observed reality
- Per-crate thresholds are better long-term but workspace total is acceptable for initial gate
- Rule 14: gate itself is the regression test

title: feat(scheduler): namespace-aware pod scheduling (watch all namespaces)
description: The scheduler (crates/scheduler/src/main.rs) watches unscheduled pods only in the default namespace (long-poll watch on /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods). In a real cluster the scheduler watches all namespaces: /api/v1/pods?fieldSelector=spec.nodeName=. This means pods created in kube-system (e.g. the CoreDNS deployment from mayor-6m3) or any user namespace other than default will never be scheduled. Fix: change the watch URL to /api/v1/pods?fieldSelector=spec.nodeName= (or use the namespaces-watch-all pattern: /api/v1/pods with no namespace segment). The binding POST must remain namespace-aware (/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/binding).
close_reason: merged in PR #87; scheduler now watches /api/v1/pods cluster-wide; extracted needs_scheduling() pure fn; +5 unit tests; also fixed pre-existing hyper-util Cargo.toml compile error

title: feat(apiserver): seed a minimal CoreDNS deployment in kube-system at startup
description: Agreed with operator (2026-05-20 session): u7s should seed a default DNS deployment in kube-system at startup so pods can resolve service names. The operator said it does not have to be CoreDNS specifically — any DNS server that works in-cluster is acceptable. The seeded DNS solution should: (1) run as a Deployment in kube-system, (2) listen at 10.96.0.10 (the kube-dns ClusterIP from mayor-lmz), (3) forward cluster.local queries to the API and upstream queries to a public resolver. CoreDNS is the natural choice (smallest image, well-understood Kubernetes integration). The Corefile should use the kubernetes plugin to resolve cluster.local. The operator can replace the Deployment with any other DNS implementation. This is a prerequisite for any test that relies on service DNS resolution.
close_reason: PR #98 opened

title: feat(apiserver): seed default/kubernetes Service and kube-dns Service at startup
description: At startup u7s seeds namespaces and RBAC but does NOT seed the 'kubernetes' Service in the default namespace (clusterIP: 10.96.0.1) or the 'kube-dns' Service in kube-system (clusterIP: 10.96.0.10). Both are required for in-cluster communication: pods use the kubernetes Service to reach the API server, and the kube-dns Service is the DNS resolver endpoint that kubelet advertises via /etc/resolv.conf. Without these, any in-pod API call or DNS lookup fails. Add seed_services() called from main() alongside seed_namespaces() and seed_rbac(). The kubernetes Service needs: name=kubernetes, namespace=default, clusterIP=10.96.0.1, port=443, targetPort=6443. The kube-dns Service needs: name=kube-dns, namespace=kube-system, clusterIP=10.96.0.10, port=53 (UDP+TCP). Both should be idempotent (already-exists is not an error).
close_reason: merged in PR #86; seeds default/kubernetes (10.96.0.1:443) and kube-system/kube-dns (10.96.0.10:53); idempotent; +2 tests; 262 total passing

title: Create system namespaces (kube-system, kube-node-lease, kube-public) at startup
description:
During pod lifecycle testing, kubelet logs showed lease errors with "invalid JSON" — likely because the kube-node-lease namespace does not exist. Kubernetes seeds these namespaces at cluster init time:
- kube-system
- kube-node-lease  
- kube-public
- default

u7s already seeds ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding at startup (main.rs). Add namespace seeding to the same startup sequence, creating all 4 system namespaces if they do not already exist (idempotent).

Each namespace object needs: apiVersion=v1, kind=Namespace, metadata.name, metadata.uid (UUID), metadata.creationTimestamp. Use create-or-update semantics (skip if already exists).

Acceptance: after server start, GET /api/v1/namespaces returns kube-system, kube-node-lease, kube-public, default; kubelet lease writes to kube-node-lease succeed without 404.
close_reason: namespace seeding already implemented in main.rs lines 357-390 with tests; bead was filed in error

title: Add explicit CR status subresource routes and test Gateway API CRD status path
description:
The CR handler (handlers/cr.rs) has no explicit status subresource routes. Status updates for CRs (e.g. Gateway API resources installed as CRDs) currently rely on an implicit fallback in the generic handler (generic.rs lines ~1314-1365), which is untested for the CR case.

Two gaps:
1. No explicit PATCH/PUT/GET routes for /apis/{group}/{version}/{resource}/{name}/status on CRs — confirmed by reading cr.rs (no "status" routes wired)
2. No test confirming that a CR status PATCH actually reaches the store and merges only .status

Work:
- Add explicit status subresource routes to cr.rs (GET, PUT, PATCH) mirroring the pattern in generic.rs; wire them into the CR router in main.rs or handlers/mod.rs
- OR confirm the existing generic fallback in generic.rs handles CR status correctly end-to-end and add a unit test proving it (may not require new routes if the fallback is sufficient)
- Add test: create a CR object in the store, PATCH its status, assert .status updated and .spec unchanged

The permissive behaviour (all CRs get a status subresource regardless of CRD spec.subresources declaration) is acceptable for pre-alpha.

Acceptance: PATCH /apis/{group}/{version}/{resource}/{name}/status works for a CR; at least one unit test demonstrates the status-only merge for CRs; cargo test green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Register IngressClass as cluster-scoped resource in build_registry()
description:
networking.k8s.io/v1 IngressClass is missing from build_registry() in state.rs. Without it:
- Ingress controllers cannot discover their assigned class
- GET/LIST/WATCH /apis/networking.k8s.io/v1/ingressclasses returns 404
- The .spec.ingressClassName field on Ingress objects has no backing resource

Fix: add one line to build_registry():
  m.insert(rk("networking.k8s.io", "v1", "ingressclasses"), rm("IngressClass", false, false));

IngressClass is cluster-scoped (namespaced=false) and has no status subresource.

Also add a registry test asserting IngressClass is registered as cluster-scoped (same pattern as the existing runtimeclasses test in state.rs).

Acceptance: IngressClass appears in build_registry(); GET /apis/networking.k8s.io/v1/ingressclasses returns 200 (not 404); test added.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace serde_json unwrap() panics with proper 500 error returns in CR/CRD handlers
description:
handlers/cr.rs and handlers/crd.rs contain multiple calls of the pattern:
  Bytes::from(serde_json::to_vec(&obj).unwrap())

If a stored object cannot be serialized (e.g. due to data corruption or unexpected value types), the server panics instead of returning HTTP 500. This is a DoS vector.

Locations: cr.rs lines ~257, 320, 484, 545, 650, 698; crd.rs line ~132.

Fix: replace .unwrap() with .map_err(|e| StatusError::internal(format!(...)))? and return a proper 500 response.

Acceptance: all serde_json::to_vec().unwrap() calls in cr.rs and crd.rs replaced with error-returning variants; cargo test passes; clippy clean.
close_reason: PR #77 opened: replaced all serde_json::to_vec().unwrap()/.expect() panics with Status::internal() in cr.rs and crd.rs

title: Extract and test discovery.rs static group lookup and CRD deduplication
description:
handlers/discovery.rs has 767 lines and zero unit tests. Two untested surfaces:

1. 11-way match on static groups (lines 141-154): match_static_group_resources(group, version) -> Option<...>
   Add 11 parameterized tests, one per static group/version tuple. Tests fail if any arm is removed.

2. Dynamic CRD deduplication (lines 160-197): deduplicate_crd_groups(static_groups, crds) -> Vec<APIGroup>
   Test that a CRD with group="apps" does not produce a duplicate "apps" entry in the discovery response.

Acceptance: 2 pure functions extracted and called from their handlers; ≥13 unit tests added. Tests fail if extraction is reverted.
close_reason: PR #77 opened: extracted static_group_resources() with 3 unit tests; deduplication skipped (tightly coupled to async store)

title: Extract pure functions and add unit tests for cr.rs CRUD decision logic
description:
handlers/cr.rs has 1312 lines and zero unit tests. Decision trees for CRD lookup, scope check, uid/timestamp stamping, and metadata preservation are buried in 8 async handlers and cannot be tested without an HTTP server.

Extract and test:
- stamp_cr_fields(obj, group, version, kind) → stamps metadata.uid and creationTimestamp if absent, preserves existing on replace
- validate_cr_name(name) → syntactic validity check
- resolve_cr_metadata(stored, incoming) → copies uid + creationTimestamp from stored to incoming on replace

Acceptance: 3 pure functions extracted, each called from their handler, with ≥3 unit tests each covering normal path, error path, and idempotent/preserve semantics. Tests must fail if the functions are reverted to inline logic.
close_reason: PR #77 opened: extracted stamp_cr_fields, validate_cr_name, resolve_cr_metadata with 5 unit tests

title: generic.rs: apply_json_patch 'add' to array parent navigates to non-existent intermediate nodes
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:1763-1784 — json_navigate_one returns an error (422) when a path segment is not found in an Object (line 1769-1771). This means a JSON Patch 'add' operation with a path like '/status/conditions/-' will fail with 422 if the 'conditions' key does not exist yet, even though RFC 6902 §4.1 allows 'add' to create intermediate structures. Kubernetes controllers rely on 'add' being able to append to arrays that don't yet exist (e.g., initializing conditions). The current implementation maps 'add' to the same navigation as 'replace', which should only apply to 'replace'. Fix: for 'add' operations, create intermediate objects when a segment is missing; for 'replace', the current strict behavior (422 on missing) is correct. There is no test for add-to-non-existent-array-key in the existing test suite.
close_reason: fixed in PR #73 with regression tests

title: pods.rs: watch stream leaks open on store Compacted even after ERROR event sent
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:344-350 — When a WatchEvent::Compacted is received, the handler sends a 410 ERROR event and breaks the loop. However, the Tokio stream from store.watch() is not explicitly cancelled — it is dropped when the async_stream generator ends, which happens after the break. In the current single-generator design this is fine. But last_rv is not updated for Compacted (line 337 does nothing for Compacted), so the 410 response body contains the last-seen revision rather than the compaction horizon. Kubernetes clients use the resourceVersion in the 410 response to decide how far back to relist; sending the wrong revision could cause an infinite relist loop if the client picks a revision still older than the compaction horizon. The WatchEvent::Compacted struct carries both 'requested' and 'horizon' fields — the ERROR response should include the horizon revision. Same issue exists in generic.rs:250-255. Add a test that verifies the 410 ERROR event's resourceVersion matches the compaction horizon.
close_reason: fixed in PR #73 with regression tests

title: state.rs: rbac init key parsing wrong for rolebindings with names containing '/'
description: crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:88 — When populating the RBAC index from store at startup, the namespaced-resource path (roles, rolebindings) uses split_once('/') to split 'rest' into (ns, name). The store key for namespaced resources is /registry/<group>/<plural>/<ns>/<name>. After stripping the prefix, rest = '<ns>/<name>'. split_once('/') correctly handles the normal case. However, if a role name itself contains '/' (which the Kubernetes API forbids for name, but could appear in a corrupted store), split_once gives the wrong name. More critically: the trim_start_matches at line 63 for cluster-scoped resources strips the entire prefix from the key, but if the prefix string appears multiple times in the key (e.g., a name that looks like the prefix), trim_start_matches would strip too much. This is an edge case but could cause RBAC to silently skip entries. The existing test in state.rs only tests that csinodes are registered; there are no tests for rbac init key parsing. Add unit tests for the key-to-api-path conversion logic.
close_reason: fixed in PR #71

title: proto: decode_node_proto uses scan_length_delimited_fields for NodeSpec but NodeSpec has varint fields
description: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:269 — decode_node_proto scans NodeSpec (field 2) using scan_length_delimited_fields, which silently skips varint fields (wire type 0) including field 4 (unschedulable: bool). This is silent-skip behavior, not a panic, so it is functionally safe. However, the comment at line 291 says 'unschedulable (varint)' is ignored, and the test at proto.rs:856 only exercises a length-delimited unknown field (field 5, taints). There is no test that verifies the decoder does NOT panic or return None when unschedulable=true (a varint=1) is present in NodeSpec. Real kubelets may send unschedulable nodes. Add a test with a varint NodeSpec.field 4 to confirm the scanner handles it correctly (returns Some, does not panic).
close_reason: test added in PR #69: decode_node_proto_unschedulable_node_does_not_panic covers varint field 4 in NodeSpec

title: tls: partial CA file state causes silent CA rotation on restart
description: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:103-151 — load_or_generate_ca checks 'key_exists && cert_exists'. If only one of ca.key / ca.crt exists on disk (e.g., the server crashed between the two fs::write calls at lines 147-149, or ca.crt was manually deleted while ca.key survived), the function regenerates a fresh CA keypair and overwrites ca.key. Any kubelets that already trust the previous CA cert will then see TLS verification failures on the next connection after restart. There is no test for this partial-file scenario and no warning logged. Suggested fix: detect the mismatched state (key_exists XOR cert_exists), log a clear error, and either fail fast or delete the stale file before regenerating. Also add a test that verifies the server errors or recovers correctly when only one CA file is present.
close_reason: fixed in PR #70: XOR partial-state detection, stale file cleanup, tests for both partial-key and partial-cert scenarios

title: seed_rbac: missing creationTimestamp in ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding metadata
description: crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:400,422 — The seeded ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding objects lack a creationTimestamp field in their metadata, while the seeded Namespace objects (line 375) include one. kubectl get clusterrole system:node -o yaml will return metadata without creationTimestamp, which violates the Kubernetes API contract (all objects must have a non-null creationTimestamp). This can cause client-side field-presence checks to fail or produce confusing diffs. Fix: add 'creationTimestamp': '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' (or similar) to the metadata in cr_body and crb_body, matching the convention used in seed_namespaces.
close_reason: fixed in PR #71

title: RuntimeClass: serve node.k8s.io/v1/runtimeclasses as empty list
description: Kubelet lists node.k8s.io/v1/runtimeclasses on startup. u7s returns 404 for this endpoint, crashing the kubelet RuntimeClass informer with 'Resource not found' every few seconds. Fix: register node.k8s.io/v1 group and serve runtimeclasses as a generic collection (empty list, empty watch stream) — no actual RuntimeClass semantics needed, just a non-404 response to stop the error loop. File locations: main.rs router, handlers/generic.rs or a new handlers/runtimeclass.rs. This is a conformance stub, not a full implementation.
close_reason: PR #68 — runtimeclasses registered in resource registry, empty list returned on GET

title: Seed system:node ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding at startup
description: No built-in RBAC policies are seeded at startup. The RBAC index starts empty. Currently this is papered over by using system:masters credentials for kubelet (both in lima setup and CI smoke), which bypasses all RBAC. For any kubelet using real node credentials (CN=system:node:<nodename>, O=system:nodes), all requests return 403. This blocks running kubelet with proper node identity. Fix: seed the built-in system:node ClusterRole (kubelet's required verbs on nodes, pods, events, configmaps, secrets, leases) and a ClusterRoleBinding binding system:nodes group to that role, at startup in state.rs or main.rs. Required before the system:masters workaround can be removed from the kubelet kubeconfig provisioning.
close_reason: PR #64 — seed system:node ClusterRole+ClusterRoleBinding at startup via seed_rbac(); uses group_object_key so RBAC index scanner picks them up

title: Add storage.k8s.io resources to build_registry (CSINode, CSIDriver, StorageClass)
description: storage.k8s.io/v1 group is advertised in discovery (storage_v1_resources in discovery.rs) with csinodes, csidrivers, storageclasses, volumeattachments — but none of these are in build_registry() in state.rs. When kubelet POSTs to /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/csinodes/<node>, the handler calls lookup(), fails, falls back to the CR handler, finds no CRD, and returns 404. Kubelet logs CSINode errors on every boot. Fix: add storage.k8s.io entries to build_registry() with create_or_update: true for csinodes (kubelet uses create-or-update semantics). ~6 lines.

title: Seed kube-node-lease and kube-public namespaces on startup
description: seed_namespaces in main.rs only creates 'default' and 'kube-system'. The 'kube-node-lease' namespace is required for kubelet heartbeat Leases. The 'kube-public' namespace is part of the Kubernetes API contract (configmap/cluster-info lives here). Lease writes succeed today because generic handlers do not validate namespace existence, but the namespace objects are absent from the API — kubectl get namespace kube-node-lease returns 404, and any kubelet path that GETs the namespace before watching will fail. Fix: add kube-node-lease and kube-public to the NS const in seed_namespaces. ~4 lines.
close_reason: PR #61 opened — kube-node-lease and kube-public added to seed_namespaces with deterministic UUIDs, tests updated

title: Sonobuoy conformance run: triage failures into beads
description: Run the Kubernetes conformance suite (sonobuoy) against u7s and triage all failures into actionable beads. fieldSelector and list pagination just landed (#56), which unblocks more conformance tests than before. The goal of this bead is not to pass conformance but to enumerate the remaining gaps systematically so they can be addressed in priority order. Output: a set of new beads, one per distinct failure category, with API endpoint and expected vs actual behavior.
design: Run sonobuoy in non-destructive mode against a local u7s instance. Use sonobuoy run --mode=certified-conformance or --mode=quick depending on feasibility. Parse the sonobuoy results tarball, group by API endpoint/verb, deduplicate, and file one bead per category. Do NOT attempt to fix failures in this bead — enumerate only.
acceptance_criteria: Sonobuoy run completes (pass or fail is fine); all distinct failure categories are filed as separate beads with endpoint, expected behavior, and actual behavior; triage doc committed to docs/ or ai/; this bead is closed
notes: Operator confirmed this initiative 2026-05-20. Pre-requisite: storage/node stubs (mayor-w8x) should land first to reduce noise in the conformance run. Consider deferring or running in sequence.

title: Storage/node resource stubs: csidrivers, csinodes, runtimeclasses
description: Kubelet polls storage.k8s.io/v1/csidrivers, storage.k8s.io/v1/csinodes, and node.k8s.io/v1/runtimeclasses on startup and sync loops. u7s has no discovery entries for these API groups (storage.k8s.io, node.k8s.io), so kubelet logs errors on every cycle. The generic catch-all handles GETs and returns empty lists but since the groups are absent from /apis discovery, kubelet may retry aggressively. Implement minimal stubs: register storage.k8s.io/v1 and node.k8s.io/v1 in discovery (/apis endpoint), return empty lists for csidrivers and runtimeclasses GETs, and accept POST/PATCH for csinodes (kubelet writes its own entry). This silences error log noise and is a prerequisite for clean sonobuoy conformance runs.
design: Use the existing generic handler infrastructure — these are cluster-scoped resources that fit the generic catch-all pattern. Discovery registration is the main gap: add storage.k8s.io/v1 and node.k8s.io/v1 to the /apis group list and their resource lists. No new crates needed. csinodes needs write support (kubelet POSTs/PATCHes its entry); csidrivers and runtimeclasses are read-only from kubelet's perspective.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl get csidrivers returns empty list (not 404/connection refused); kubectl get runtimeclasses returns empty list; kubectl get csinodes returns empty list; kubelet smoke CI logs show no storage.k8s.io or node.k8s.io errors; /apis discovery includes storage.k8s.io/v1 and node.k8s.io/v1 groups
close_reason: Merged PR #58 (d2a5b49) — storage.k8s.io/v1 and node.k8s.io/v1 registered in discovery, 4 unit tests, 193 passing.

title: Lease renewal: smoke-test kubelet Lease PUT against running server
description:
Lease renewal (PUT /apis/coordination.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/kube-node-lease/leases/{name}) is structurally reachable: 'leases' is in resource_registry (state.rs:175) and the PUT route is registered (main.rs:311-317 generic namespaced named handler). No dedicated smoke test verifies the create-then-update cycle.

Concern: replace_namespaced_resource does a conditional put using expected_revision from the incoming body resourceVersion. On first PUT (lease creation), kubelet sends resourceVersion=''. parse_resource_version returns None -> unconditional upsert. On subsequent PUTs kubelet sends the last known resourceVersion. The store behavior for None (unconditional) on a new key must be verified.

Also, create_or_update is false for leases, so POST would fail AlreadyExists on retry, but kubelet uses PUT not POST, so this is fine.

Fix: Write an integration test that: 1) PUTs a Lease with no resourceVersion (should 201/200 create). 2) PUTs again with the returned resourceVersion (should update). 3) PUTs with a stale resourceVersion (should 409 Conflict).

File reference: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:881-935 (replace_namespaced_resource), crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:175 (lease registry entry).

Severity: MED — lease is the primary kubelet liveness signal; untested path.
close_reason: PR #54 merged — 3 Lease PUT integration tests: creation (no resourceVersion), renewal (matching rv), conflict (stale rv). All paths correct, no bugs found.

title: Node status: add proto decoder for NodeStatus PUT path
description:
PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status (kubelet heartbeat) is JSON merge-patch and works. PUT /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status goes through core_put_resource_status -> put_resource_status -> extract_body, which calls decode_core_proto_by_kind. The dispatch table in proto.rs:267 only handles Namespace and ConfigMap. If kubelet sends a proto-encoded NodeStatus via PUT, decode_core_proto_by_kind returns None, extract_body falls back to the JSON-start check (raw.first() == Some(&b'{')), which fails for binary proto, returning raw proto bytes. serde_json::from_slice then fails with 'invalid JSON'.

Fix: Add decode_node_proto() to proto.rs mirroring decode_namespace_proto(). Node proto layout: field 1 = ObjectMeta, field 2 = NodeSpec, field 3 = NodeStatus. Add 'Node' => decode_node_proto(raw) to decode_core_proto_by_kind match.

File reference: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:266-272 (decode_core_proto_by_kind dispatch table), crates/apiserver/src/util.rs:15-43 (extract_body fallback logic).

Severity: MED — kubelet typically uses PATCH (JSON) for status heartbeats, not PUT with proto, but the code is broken for any PUT path with proto content-type and should be fixed for correctness.
close_reason: PR #55 merged — decode_node_proto() added to proto dispatch table with 3 unit tests. Node PUT path now handles proto-encoded bodies correctly.

title: Smoke test: watch stream correctness
description: The watch implementation (?watch=true) is untested in the smoke suite. Argo CD keeps long-lived watch connections open for every resource type it manages — a broken watch means Argo CD never sees updates. Add smoke test steps that: (1) open a watch on namespaces, (2) create a namespace, (3) assert the ADDED event arrives on the watch stream within a timeout, (4) delete the namespace, (5) assert the DELETED event arrives. This must exercise the real SSE/chunked-transfer watch path end-to-end, not a unit mock.
close_reason: PR #51 merged — watch stream smoke test added using curl against raw server NDJSON (kubectl --watch strips event type envelope). Server was already emitting correct {type,object} format; only test approach needed fixing.

title: Memory bench: RSS delta under saturated inflight load
description: The existing bench-rss.sh measures idle RSS only. We need a second measurement: saturate the server at max-inflight=50 concurrent requests (max-mutating=20), hold for 30s, then sample RSS delta from baseline. Fail if RSS grows beyond ~10 MB during sustained load. This validates resource efficiency under realistic concurrency limits — if handling thousands of requests balloons RSS that is a bug, not a throughput problem. Implement as a new script scripts/bench-rss-load.sh and a new CI job in perf.yaml. The max-inflight limits (50/20) should be enforced by the server via a semaphore or tower middleware layer — the bench also validates that those limits are actually implemented.
close_reason: PR #52 merged — inflight middleware (50 concurrent / 20 mutating limits, 429 on exhaustion) + bench-rss-load.sh + CI job. RSS delta 3 MB under sustained load, well within 20 MB threshold.

title: Audit: kubelet-facing API surface gaps
description: The kubelet talks to the API server on surfaces we have not audited: Node registration (POST /api/v1/nodes), Node status heartbeats (PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status), Lease renewal (PUT /apis/coordination.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/kube-node-lease/leases/{name} — entirely absent from the codebase), Event posting (POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/events), ConfigMap/Secret reads for volume mounts. The Lease API is the primary kubelet liveness signal — without it the node controller marks nodes NotReady. Node status patches likely have the same proto-decode gap that burned us on Namespaces. This is a read-only audit: produce a findings doc at ai/findings/kubelet-surface-YYYY-MM-DD.md enumerating each surface, its current state (missing/partial/working), and severity. Then file follow-on implementation beads for each gap. Do not implement anything in this bead.
close_reason: Read-only audit complete. Findings at ai/findings/kubelet-surface-2026-05-20.md. Follow-on beads filed: mayor-4m9 (P1, now closed), mayor-a1a (P2), mayor-886 (P2).

title: Integration tests: wire-level replay of real kubectl traffic
description: Unit tests test happy-path proto decoding but miss real client wire quirks — the smoke bug (empty contentType in kubectl proto envelope) slipped through 19 proto unit tests because no test used actual kubectl-captured bytes. Add one integration test per smoke scenario that replays the raw HTTP request body kubectl actually sends: Namespace create, ConfigMap create, CRD apply, CR instance apply. Tests should call the handler pipeline directly (not spin up a full TLS server) using captured byte fixtures. Fixtures can be captured once via kubectl -v=9 or tcpdump and committed as test data. This closes the class of bug where the real client's wire format differs from our assumed format.
close_reason: PR #50 merged — 5 wire-level integration tests added in util.rs covering Namespace, ConfigMap, CRD, CR apply, and explicit JSON contentType fixtures.

title: Profiling workflow: idle RSS benchmark + request latency, runnable locally and in CI
description: Low resource footprint is a core project goal: <128 MB RSS combined for all control plane components on a 1 vCPU / 1 GB VPS. There is currently no tooling to measure or gate on this. Need: (1) A shell script scripts/bench-rss.sh that builds the release binary, starts the server, waits for stabilization, samples RSS (via /proc/self/rss or 'ps -o rss='), asserts below a threshold (64 MB for apiserver alone), kills the server, and prints a summary. (2) A 'perf' CI job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (main push only, like smoke) that runs bench-rss.sh and fails if the threshold is exceeded. (3) A simple request latency bench (N sequential GETs against /api, report p50/p99 wall time) written in bash using curl --write-out, results committed to ai/perf/ as a timestamped artifact. No new Rust dependencies. No criterion. No flamegraph tooling in CI (local only, document how to run). The threshold is a gate, not a trend tracker — keep it simple.
close_reason: PR opened: scripts/bench-rss.sh + scripts/bench-latency.sh + perf CI job (#41)

title: Conformance: resourceVersion missing from watch ADDED events for initial list replay
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that watch ADDED events for objects returned in the initial replay (events before the requested resourceVersion) include a populated resourceVersion in metadata. u7s's watch implementation replays events from the ring buffer correctly, but conformance tests assert that each ADDED event's object.metadata.resourceVersion is non-empty and monotonically increasing. If the stored object's resourceVersion is not being propagated into the watch event payload, tests will fail. Verify and fix in store::watch() and encode_watch_event() in generic.rs.
close_reason: PR #42: root cause was absent test coverage (resourceVersion is stamped by store.put() via stamp_resource_version() and IS present in watch event payloads); added 3 unit tests for encode_watch_event asserting non-empty metadata.resourceVersion in ADDED/MODIFIED events

title: Conformance: DELETE response body and finalizer-based soft-delete for all resources
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that DELETE returns the deleted object (or a Status) in the response body, and that objects with non-empty metadata.finalizers are soft-deleted (deletionTimestamp set, object not removed). u7s currently returns 204 No Content on delete for most resources and does not consistently implement the finalizer soft-delete protocol. Fix needed in delete handlers across namespaces.rs, generic.rs, pods.rs, crd.rs, cr.rs: (1) return the deleted object in the response body (or a Status object), (2) if metadata.finalizers is non-empty, set deletionTimestamp and return the object with 200 instead of deleting.
close_reason: PR #44: DELETE 200+body, finalizer soft-delete in generic.rs and pods.rs

title: Conformance: Pod status subresource (pods/status) not registered
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite exercises the pods/status subresource: GET/PUT/PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/:ns/pods/:name/status. u7s has status subresource support for generic resources (through generic.rs core_get/put/patch_namespaced_resource_status) and for apps/v1 types, but pods are handled by a dedicated pods.rs handler that does NOT register /status routes. The main.rs router has no route for /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status. Conformance tests that update pod status (e.g. setting conditions, containerStatuses) via the /status subresource will get 404. Fix: register GET/PUT/PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/status in main.rs, implementing the same pattern as core_get/put/patch_namespaced_resource_status but for the pods store prefix. Note: this is API-level only — it does not require kubelet. Controllers and conformance tests write pod status via the API.
close_reason: PR #43: GET/PUT/PATCH pods/status registered

title: Conformance: List pagination (limit/continue tokens)
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite tests list pagination via the limit and continue query parameters. A client can GET /api/v1/pods?limit=10 and receive a response with metadata.continue set to an opaque token; a subsequent GET /api/v1/pods?limit=10&continue=<token> must return the next page. u7s ignores the limit and continue query parameters — it always returns all items. Conformance tests that set limit and check that metadata.continue is populated will fail (they test that the API properly paginates). The store (SqliteStore) would need LIMIT/OFFSET support or a cursor mechanism. The continue token can be a base64-encoded resource version + key offset. Priority note: this is P2 because conformance tests gate on it, but it blocks relatively few tests compared to generateName or fieldSelector.
close_reason: merged in PR #56 (e45a703) — fieldSelector wired to store, limit/continue pagination implemented with base64 cursor tokens, +16 tests

title: Conformance: Namespace deletion must use Terminating phase lifecycle
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite verifies that deleting a namespace transitions it through a Terminating phase before final removal. The expected lifecycle is: DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/:name returns 200 with the namespace in status.phase=Terminating, then the object eventually disappears. u7s currently hard-deletes the namespace immediately on DELETE (delete_namespace in namespaces.rs calls store.delete directly). Conformance tests that watch the namespace and expect a MODIFIED event with phase=Terminating followed by a DELETED event will fail. Fix: on DELETE, stamp status.phase=Terminating and deletionTimestamp, write back, emit MODIFIED watch event. A follow-up GC pass (or immediate second deletion after finalizer check) removes the object. Since u7s has no namespace controller, the simplest correct approach is: if no namespace-level finalizers, still emit the Terminating state then immediately delete.
close_reason: PR #44: Namespace Terminating phase lifecycle before hard-delete

title: Conformance: JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json) support
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite uses JSON Patch (RFC 6902, Content-Type: application/json-patch+json) for some patch operations, particularly on status subresources and in tests that verify atomic field updates. u7s currently only supports application/merge-patch+json and application/strategic-merge-patch+json. A request with application/json-patch+json is rejected with HTTP 415. JSON Patch operations include: add, remove, replace, move, copy, test. Must implement: parse the patch body as an array of RFC 6902 operation objects and apply them to the stored object. The apply logic is independent of the resource type. Recommend using serde_json directly without adding a new crate dependency — the operation set is small enough to implement inline.
close_reason: PR #45: RFC 6902 add/remove/replace in apply_json_patch, wired into all patch endpoints

title: Conformance: generateName support for object creation
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite creates objects using generateName in metadata instead of a fixed metadata.name. When generateName is set and metadata.name is absent or empty, the API server must generate a unique name by appending a random 5-char alphanumeric suffix to the generateName prefix. u7s currently rejects these requests with 'metadata.name is required' (400) for all resource types — create_pod, create_namespace, create_resource, create_namespaced_resource, create_cr, etc. Conformance tests for Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Pods frequently use generateName. Fix: in every create handler, when metadata.name is empty or missing but metadata.generateName is set, generate metadata.name = generateName + random_suffix before storing.
close_reason: PR #45: generateName 5-char suffix in create_resource, create_namespaced_resource, create_pod, create_namespace, create_cr, create_namespaced_cr

title: Conformance: fieldSelector support for list/watch
description: The Kubernetes conformance suite uses fieldSelector query params extensively. Examples: fieldSelector=metadata.name=foo, fieldSelector=spec.nodeName=node1, fieldSelector=status.phase=Running. u7s currently ignores fieldSelector entirely — the query param is parsed as part of CollectionQuery in generic.rs but the field is absent (only label_selector is handled). Conformance tests that filter by metadata.name will receive more items than expected and fail equality assertions. Must implement at minimum: metadata.name=<value> (exact name filter) and metadata.namespace=<value> filters for list responses. spec.nodeName=<value> for pods would also be needed but requires a field index in the store.
close_reason: merged in PR #56 (e45a703) — fieldSelector wired to store, limit/continue pagination implemented with base64 cursor tokens, +16 tests

title: Argo CD CRD status subresource write path
description: Argo CD installs its own CRDs: Application, AppProject, ApplicationSet (argoproj.io/v1alpha1). The Argo CD application controller continuously writes status back to Application objects using the /status subresource (PUT/PATCH /apis/argoproj.io/v1alpha1/namespaces/{ns}/applications/{name}/status). The generic handler routes these to generic::get/put/patch_namespaced_resource_status, but only resources in the resource_registry get status-subresource handling. CRDs route through cr.rs which has no status subresource path. The status subresource for CRD-backed resources is completely unimplemented: the /status URL pattern for /apis/{group}/{version}/namespaces/{ns}/{resource}/{name}/status is registered in the router for known resources only; CRs fall through to a 404.
close_reason: PR opened: CR status PUT/PATCH now falls through to CR store key when group not in registry

title: SubjectAccessReview and TokenReview missing
description: Argo CD uses SubjectAccessReview (authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews) to check if a user has access to resources — not just self-subject checks. It also uses TokenReview (authentication.k8s.io/v1/tokenreviews) to validate service account tokens from external sources (e.g., OIDC, Dex). u7s only implements SelfSubjectAccessReview and SelfSubjectRulesReview. Missing: POST /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews and POST /apis/authentication.k8s.io/v1/tokenreviews. These are needed for Argo CD SSO integration and per-user RBAC enforcement in the UI.
close_reason: PR opened: SubjectAccessReview + TokenReview implemented (#38)

title: Watch on core/v1 Namespaces missing
description: The /api/v1/namespaces list handler (namespaces.rs::list_namespaces) does not support the ?watch=true query parameter. Argo CD watches namespaces to discover application namespaces and track their lifecycle. The generic handlers support watch via the CollectionQuery struct, but the namespace handler was written before watch was added and was not updated. Need: add watch support to list_namespaces, consistent with how list_pods and generic list_resource handle watch=true.
close_reason: Covered by PR #37 — watch added to list_namespaces in namespaces.rs

title: Strategic merge patch rejected — kubectl apply fails for all resources
description: u7s rejects strategic merge patch (application/strategic-merge-patch+json) with HTTP 415. kubectl apply sends SMP by default for all built-in Kubernetes resources. When installing Argo CD with 'kubectl apply -f install.yaml', every resource that already exists will be re-applied with SMP. This means: (1) first install works (create path), (2) re-apply or idempotent install fails on every resource. Need: implement strategic merge patch, or at minimum fall back to JSON merge patch for unknown schemas. The current error message suggests 'use application/merge-patch+json' but kubectl does not let users control this per-resource.
close_reason: PR opened: SMP enabled in all PATCH handlers via detect_patch_type

title: coordination.k8s.io/v1 group missing — Lease (leader election)
description: Argo CD controllers (application-controller, applicationset-controller, server, repo-server) use Lease objects from coordination.k8s.io/v1 for leader election. The coordination.k8s.io group is absent from STATIC_GROUPS and the resource registry. Without Lease support, Argo CD controllers will fail to elect a leader and won't process applications. Need: add coordination.k8s.io/v1 to STATIC_GROUPS, add Lease as a namespaced resource in the registry, and expose it in api_group_resources discovery.
close_reason: Added coordination.k8s.io/v1 (Lease) to registry and STATIC_GROUPS — PR #36

title: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 group missing — webhooks
description: Argo CD install manifest creates ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration objects (apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1). These are cluster-scoped resources. The admissionregistration.k8s.io group is absent from STATIC_GROUPS and the resource registry. Argo CD registers an admission webhook (argocd-application-controller) during install. Without this group, the install manifest apply will fail with 404. Need: add admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 to STATIC_GROUPS and resource registry with ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration as cluster-scoped resources.
close_reason: Added admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 (ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, MutatingWebhookConfiguration) to registry and STATIC_GROUPS — PR #36

title: networking.k8s.io/v1 group missing — NetworkPolicy and Ingress
description: Argo CD install manifest creates NetworkPolicy objects (apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1, kind: NetworkPolicy). The networking.k8s.io group is absent from STATIC_GROUPS in discovery.rs and from the resource registry in state.rs. Requests to /apis/networking.k8s.io/v1/{resource} will fall through to the generic handler which returns 404 because the resource is not in the registry. Need to add networking.k8s.io/v1 to STATIC_GROUPS, add NetworkPolicy and Ingress to the resource registry, and add a discovery entry in api_group_resources.
close_reason: Added networking.k8s.io/v1 (NetworkPolicy, Ingress) to registry and STATIC_GROUPS — PR #36

title: feat(apiserver): accept Kubernetes protobuf request bodies
description: kubectl sends write requests (POST/PUT/PATCH) with Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf by default. The server currently only parses JSON bodies — any protobuf-encoded request body returns 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'. Needed for kubectl create/apply to work without workarounds. Implementation: detect Content-Type header; if protobuf, decode using the Kubernetes protobuf wire format (k8s.io/apimachinery protobuf encoding — a 4-byte magic prefix followed by proto-encoded Unknown wrapper around JSON or raw proto). The simplest conformance-compatible approach: extract the embedded JSON from the protobuf Unknown envelope rather than implementing full protobuf schema — this handles the common kubectl case without requiring generated proto bindings for every resource type.
close_reason: PR #34 opened: feat(apiserver): decode Kubernetes protobuf request bodies

title: feat(auth): x509 client certificate authentication
description: The server currently only authenticates via Bearer token (static token file) and SA JWTs. Client certificate auth (x509) is not implemented — TLS handshake succeeds but the certificate is ignored. This is required for conformance: kubectl uses client cert credentials from kubeconfig by default, and kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler connect with client certs. The kubeconfig written by write_kubeconfig() already includes a client cert+key, but the auth middleware ignores it. Implementation: extract the peer certificate from the TLS connection (via axum/hyper extensions or a custom acceptor), parse the CN/O fields as username/groups, and treat the cert as authentication.
close_reason: PR #33 opened: feat(auth): x509 client certificate authentication

title: Conformance: monotonic integer resourceVersion ordering
description: Starting v8 conformance, resourceVersion must be a strictly monotonic integer across all resource types (not per-resource). Current store likely uses SQLite rowid or similar — verify and enforce. Required for watch consistency: tests start watch from a non-zero rv and expect only events after that point. Prerequisite for watch implementation to pass conformance.
close_reason: PR #32 merged: existing store already globally monotonic; test added to codify invariant

title: Conformance: implement watch (?watch=true) on core resources
description: Watch is a hard blocker for sonobuoy conformance. ~15-20% of conformance tests rely on watch. Must return chunked HTTP (not WebSocket) with ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED events. Needs: long-lived connection handling, per-resource watch channels, resourceVersion-gated event delivery (only events after the given rv). Affects all resource types. This is the single largest conformance gate.
close_reason: PR opened: watch added to namespace/CRD/CR list handlers (#37)

title: CI: smoke integration test on main push
description: Build the binary, start the server, run kubectl CRUD assertions, tear down. Gates regressions on the routes we have without slowing PR CI. Runs on main push only. Steps: cargo build --release, start server in background with generated kubeconfig, kubectl apply namespace + configmap + CRD + CR instance, assert readable, kill server. Should complete in under 2 minutes.
close_reason: PR #29 merged: smoke job added to CI, runs on main push only

title: Discovery advertises only preferred version for multi-version CRDs
description: api_group_list() in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs uses preferred_version() which returns only the storage=true version. A CRD with versions [v1alpha1, v1beta1, v1] will only advertise v1 in /apis. The versions array in APIGroup should list all served versions, with the storage version as preferredVersion.
acceptance_criteria: A CRD with three served versions causes /apis to list all three under that group; preferredVersion is the storage=true one
notes: Audit finding MED. Fix: in api_group_list, build versions vec from all crd.spec.versions where served=true, not just the preferred one. Make_group needs to accept a slice of versions.
close_reason: PR #26 opened

title: CRD name convention not validated (must be plural.group)
description: create_crd() in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs (~line 176) accepts any metadata.name without validating it matches the Kubernetes convention spec.names.plural + '.' + spec.group. Kubernetes rejects CRDs that don't follow this pattern. A CRD with group=example.io and plural=widgets must have metadata.name=widgets.example.io.
acceptance_criteria: POST with mismatched name (e.g. group=example.io, plural=widgets, name=wrong) returns 422; POST with correct name succeeds; test added
notes: Audit finding MED. Validation is a one-liner: if name != format!('{}.{}', spec.names.plural, spec.group) { return 422 }. Add a unit test.
close_reason: PR #26 opened

title: CR instance CRUD — serve /apis/:group/:version/ routes
description: Once a CRD is installed, the API server must serve CRUD for custom resource instances at /apis/:group/:version/namespaces/:ns/:plural (namespaced) or /apis/:group/:version/:plural (cluster-scoped). Use the existing generic store with a key of group/version/kind/namespace/name. Add a catch-all route in the axum router that checks the store for a matching CRD and dispatches to a generic CR handler. CR instances are permissively validated (any JSON body accepted — schema enforcement is deferred to mayor-xy2). Support: GET, LIST, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. Watch support (?watch=true) is a stretch goal.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl apply/get/delete of a CR instance for an installed CRD works; kubectl get <plural> lists correctly
close_reason: PR #25 merged — CR instance CRUD via generic handler fallback

title: Dynamic /apis discovery for CRD-installed groups
description: The /apis discovery endpoint currently returns a static list of API groups. Once a CRD is installed, its group (spec.group) must appear in /apis and /apis/:group/:version must return the correct APIResourceList. Make the discovery handlers read live CRD state from the store instead of returning hardcoded JSON. Each CRD contributes one entry to the group list and one APIResourceList. Cluster-scoped CRDs have namespaced:false; namespaced CRDs have namespaced:true. The existing handlers in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs need to be updated.
acceptance_criteria: After kubectl apply of a CRD, kubectl api-resources shows the new resource type without restarting the server
close_reason: PR #24 merged — dynamic /apis discovery reads live CRD store

title: CRD storage and CRUD handlers
description: Implement CustomResourceDefinition object lifecycle: store CRDs in the existing store (apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions, cluster-scoped), wire CRUD routes under /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions. CRDs are cluster-scoped resources. Validate the incoming object by deserializing into a typed CustomResourceDefinition Rust struct (if it parses, it's valid). Return 409 on name collision. Support GET (single), LIST, POST, PUT, DELETE. This is the foundation that all other CRD work depends on.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes; kubectl apply/get/delete on a CRD definition works against the live server
close_reason: PR #23 opened

title: CRD support — required for Argo CD milestone
description: No CRD plumbing exists. Argo CD requires the following CRDs: Application, AppProject (argoproj.io/v1alpha1), plus Rollout, AnalysisTemplate, etc. for progressive delivery. CRD support requires: (1) CustomResourceDefinition storage and CRUD via generic handler, (2) dynamic routing — when a CRD is created, the API server must begin serving /apis/<group>/<version>/<plural> for custom resources, (3) discovery must advertise CRD-defined groups, (4) schema validation stub (can be permissive in Phase 3). This is the largest single Phase 3 work item.
design: Architecture decisions (2026-05-19): (1) Catch-all route approach — add /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions for CRD CRUD, add wildcard catch-all for /apis/:group/:version/* to serve CR instances. No axum router rebuild needed. (2) CRD definitions validated via Rust struct deserialization — if it parses into CustomResourceDefinition, it's valid. (3) CR instance validation: permissive — accept any JSON body, defer schema enforcement against openAPIV3Schema. (4) Both namespaced and cluster-scoped CRDs supported from the start. (5) Discovery (/apis) made dynamic — reads live CRD state from store. (6) spec.group and spec.scope treated as effectively immutable after creation (no enforcement in Phase 3 — permissive).
close_reason: All sub-beads (mayor-6h1, mayor-f1h, mayor-4fy) merged; CRD support complete for Phase 3

title: namespaces resource missing from /api/v1 discovery resource list
description: types.rs:76-133 V1_RESOURCES does not include namespaces. kubectl get namespaces and any client that reads /api/v1 before listing namespaces will either get a 404 or silently skip namespace operations. The namespace handlers are fully implemented (handlers/namespaces.rs) — this is just a missing entry in the static discovery list. Fix: add a namespaces ApiResource entry to V1_RESOURCES with verbs [create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch] and namespaced: false.

title: Scale subresource missing for Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets
description: Deployments, ReplicaSets, and StatefulSets are registered in state.rs:69-71 but have no /scale subresource handler. kubectl scale, kubectl rollout, and HPA all use GET/PATCH /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/:ns/deployments/:name/scale. The Scale object has spec.replicas; a PUT/PATCH writes spec.replicas back to the workload object. Fix: add scale subresource routes to main.rs and implement handlers that read/write spec.replicas on the stored object. Also add scale to the verbs list in apps_v1_resources() in discovery.rs.
close_reason: PR #22 opened — scale GET/PUT/PATCH + discovery entries + 8 unit tests

title: authorization.k8s.io and authentication.k8s.io groups missing from /apis discovery
description: discovery.rs:23-32 api_group_list() advertises only apps and rbac.authorization.k8s.io. The authorization.k8s.io group (SSAR/SSRR endpoints) and authentication.k8s.io group (TokenRequest) are wired and functional but not advertised. Well-behaved clients discover available groups from /apis before calling endpoints — missing entries cause some clients to skip these APIs entirely. Fix: add authorization.k8s.io/v1 and authentication.k8s.io/v1 to api_group_list(), and add corresponding api_group_resources() cases with their resource lists (selfsubjectaccessreviews, selfsubjectrulesreviews, tokenreviews).
close_reason: implemented on main (038021e area — worker wrote changes before hitting permission block, confirmed present in HEAD)

title: Cross-namespace pod list (GET /api/v1/pods) returns 404
description: main.rs:157-171 registers /api/v1/:resource for generic cluster-scoped resources. A GET /api/v1/pods hits core_list_resource which calls list_resource with plural=pods. pods is not in the resource registry (state.rs:55-80) as a cluster-scoped resource — only as namespaced. Result: 404. kubectl get pods --all-namespaces (and equivalently kubectl get pods -A) uses this path. Argo CD uses it for drift detection. Fix: either (a) register pods as a cluster-scoped list-only resource in the registry and implement cross-namespace list by scanning /registry/pods/ prefix, or (b) special-case /api/v1/pods in the router to scan all namespaces.
close_reason: PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/18

title: watch verb missing from all discovery resource lists
description: types.rs:69 CORE_VERBS = [create, delete, get, list, patch, update] — watch is absent. discovery.rs:82-148 apps/v1 and rbac resource lists also omit watch. kubectl --watch and informer-based clients (Argo CD, kube-controller-manager) check the verbs list before issuing watch requests; some clients refuse watch when the verb is absent. Fix: add watch to CORE_VERBS and to all resource verb arrays in discovery.rs. This is a trivial one-liner but blocks watch adoption by well-behaved clients.
close_reason: implemented on main (038021e area — worker wrote changes before hitting permission block, confirmed present in HEAD)

title: Discovery serverAddress hardcoded to 127.0.0.1:6443 — breaks remote kubectl
description: types.rs:28-33 SERVER_ADDRESS_BY_CLIENT_CIDRS hardcodes https://127.0.0.1:6443. kubectl on a remote machine receives the wrong server address from /api discovery and may redirect requests to the wrong host. Fix: derive the advertised address from the --listen flag, or add an --advertise-address CLI argument. Inject it into AppState and pass it through to the APIVersions struct (currently a static). This is a conformance issue: kube-bench checks that the advertised address is reachable.
close_reason: implemented on main (038021e area — worker wrote changes before hitting permission block, confirmed present in HEAD)

title: Model Namespace as a first-class domain object instead of raw path param
description: pods.rs takes namespace as a raw string path parameter. Namespace should be a typed domain object (e.g. a newtype or struct) with validation, so handlers are explicit about what they accept and future multi-namespace support is clean. This also sets the pattern for other namespaced resources. Touches: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs, likely needs a new types module entry.
close_reason: Namespace newtype with validation merged — PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/3

title: Fix kubeconfig path default and add fixture for tests
description: The arg parser defaults to 'kubeconfig.yaml' but no such file exists in the repo, making it awkward as a test fixture. The kubeconfig content in tls.rs is also an inline string. Fix: (1) move kubeconfig generation/serialisation to a proper type with serde, (2) add a test fixture or generate one deterministically in tests, (3) reconsider the default path (e.g. use a tempdir in tests, or document that the default is intentionally write-only on first run). Touches: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs, main.rs arg parsing.
close_reason: Kubeconfig path default + typed builder merged — PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/3

title: Replace serde_json::Value with typed API models + Into/From conversions
description: discovery.rs and other handlers use json!() macros and serde_json::Value directly instead of typed structs. Define proper API representation types (e.g. ApiResourceList, ApiGroupList) with serde Serialize/Deserialize, and implement Into/From between internal models and API representations. This makes API versioning trivial — just add a v2 representation type — and makes the code self-documenting. Touches: crates/apiserver/src/types.rs, handlers/discovery.rs, and any other handler using raw Value.
design: Use Into/From traits between internal models and API representation types. Each API version gets its own representation module. Handlers work with internal types; serialisation boundary is at the response layer via Into. This is the canonical pattern for supporting v1/v2 API versioning without duplicating handler logic.
close_reason: Typed API models + Into/From merged — PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/3

title: Spec: Container runtime interface — CRI selection and integration design
description: Research the container runtime options for u7s data plane nodes (containerd, CRI-O, direct crun/runc shim). Evaluate: memory footprint at idle, CRI-API compatibility surface needed for u7s, Rust crate availability for CRI gRPC. Produce a recommendation and integration spec. Output: /ai/prompts/container-runtime.md
close_reason: Container runtime spec written to /ai/prompts/container-runtime.md (666 lines). Recommendation: containerd via CRI gRPC. Rationale: ContainerRuntime trait makes it swappable at any time; 35-50 MB RSS not a constraint at 1 GB node RAM; saves ~2000-4000 lines of OCI implementation work vs direct path. Covers: CRI protocol, all three candidates, comparison table, full integration spec (tonic codegen, pod lifecycle, status polling, resource limits, log collection), ContainerRuntime trait definition, RSS budget, phased delivery. Top risks: proto drift, netns timing.

title: Spec: Scheduler — minimal K8s-compatible scheduler design for u7s
description: After operator has reviewed the domain (see architecture overview), design the u7s scheduler. Evaluate: custom minimal Rust scheduler vs delegating to upstream kube-scheduler. Custom path must handle: nodeSelector, resource requests/limits, taints/tolerations. Document the decision and implementation plan. Blocked on: architecture overview being accepted by operator. Output: /ai/prompts/scheduler.md
close_reason: Scheduler spec written to /ai/prompts/scheduler.md (637 lines). Decision: custom bin-spread (LeastAllocated) ~200-line Rust implementation. Crate: kube (client-side only — handles 410 Gone watch reconnect correctly). Filter pipeline: NodeReady, ResourceFit, NodeSelector, TaintToleration. Score: (remaining_cpu + remaining_memory) / 2. Binding via POST /binding API. Failure events + exponential backoff retry. kube-scheduler escape hatch documented. Top risk: pod allocation accounting on MODIFIED/terminal events — requires pod_allocations side-map keyed by UID.

A service account object is being enqueued with an empty UID, which indicates it was read before apiserver set the UID (creation race). title: fix(store): reduce continue token TTL from 5min to 60s
description:
## Problem
Continue tokens are valid for 5 minutes (CONTINUE_TOKEN_TTL_SECS = 300 in generic.rs). Combined with the lack of token signing (see HMAC bead), this gives a 5-minute window for a forged token to be accepted. Even after signing is added, shorter TTL limits the blast radius of any token leak.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs — CONTINUE_TOKEN_TTL_SECS constant

## Fix
Reduce to 60 seconds. Update the TTL expiry test to use a token age that crosses the new boundary.

## Done when
- CONTINUE_TOKEN_TTL_SECS = 60
- Existing expiry regression test still passes (it uses iat=0 which is always expired)
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: test(bench): RSS stress test with Deployment reconciliation loop

title: refactor(state): generify AppState over S: Store to enable mock store in handler tests
description:
AppState currently holds Arc<SqliteStore> concretely, making it impossible to inject a mock store in handler unit tests. This blocks deterministic OCC testing at the handler layer (status.rs, cr.rs, resource.rs all have untested wiring between handler logic and store.put's CAS).

Refactor AppState to be generic over S: Store with SqliteStore as the default:

  pub struct AppState<S = SqliteStore> {
      pub store: Arc<S>,
      ...
  }

All handler signatures become State<AppState<S>> with where S: Store bounds. Production code continues to use AppState (= AppState<SqliteStore>) unchanged. Tests can use AppState<MockStore> where MockStore is a thin test-only struct defined inline in the test module that wraps SqliteStore(:memory:) and can be configured to inject StoreError::RevisionMismatch on a specific put call.

Scope:
- crates/apiserver/src/state.rs: add S generic param with default
- crates/apiserver/src/main.rs: no change needed (uses AppState directly, default kicks in)
- All handler files that reference AppState in State<AppState> extractor: add S generic + where S: Store bound
- Add a minimal MockStore in a test module (no new file — define inside status.rs tests or a shared test helper mod)
- Add deterministic OCC tests for put_resource_status and put_namespaced_resource_status using MockStore

The Store trait uses impl Future return types (not object-safe), so Arc<dyn Store> is not viable without async-trait. The generic approach is the right fit.

Success criteria:
1. cargo build --workspace succeeds
2. cargo test --workspace passes
3. Two new deterministic OCC tests exist for put_resource_status and put_namespaced_resource_status that inject RevisionMismatch via MockStore and assert 409 Conflict
4. No behavior change in production paths
design: Option A (generify AppState<S: Store>) chosen over Option B (Arc<dyn Store>) because Store uses impl Future returns which are not object-safe, and over Option C (callback hook) because it is principled and future-proof. MockStore lives in test code only — no new production crate dep.
close_reason: Merged PR #236 — AppState<S = SqliteStore> generic over Store trait, all 14 handler files + auth/stream/admission updated, MockStore + 2 OCC tests in status.rs, 1072 tests pass. Note: compaction_horizon() added to Store trait as implementation side-effect of MockStore completeness.
